52069.e: The Monte Rosa massif lies on the border between Switzerland and Italy.
52069.m: Monte Rosa lies on the border with Italy.

52070.q: Which famous mountain stands near Zermatt, not far from the Dufourspitze?
52070.e: The Dufourspitze and the Matterhorn both stand near Zermatt in Valais.
52070.m: The Matterhorn and the Dufourspitze stand near Zermatt.

52071.q: In which country is the summit of the Dufourspitze?
52071.e: The summit of the Dufourspitze lies entirely in Switzerland, just next to the border with Italy.
52071.m: The summit of the Dufourspitze is in Switzerland.

52072.q: Between which cantons does the summit of the Jungfrau lie?
52072.e: The border between the cantons of Bern and Valais runs over the summit of the Jungfrau.
52072.m: The Jungfrau lies between Bern and Valais.

52073.q: About how high is the Jungfrau?
52073.e: The Jungfrau is about 4158 metres high, which makes it a four-thousander.
52073.m: The Jungfrau is over 4000 metres high.

52074.q: Which three mountains stand side by side in the Bernese Oberland?
52074.e: The Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau together form a famous mountain chain in the Bernese Oberland.
52074.m: The Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau stand side by side.

52075.q: In which region of Switzerland is the Jungfrau?
52075.e: The Jungfrau is one of the best-known mountains in the Bernese Oberland.
52075.m: The Jungfrau is a mountain in the Bernese Oberland.

52076.q: In which year was the Jungfrau first climbed?
52076.e: In 1811, the Meyer brothers from Aarau were the first to reach the summit.
52076.m: The Jungfrau was first climbed in 1811.

52077.q: Which town in the Bernese Oberland lies between two lakes and is known for its view of the Jungfrau?
52077.e: Interlaken lies between Lake Thun and Lake Brienz. You can see the Jungfrau well from there.
52077.m: You can see the Jungfrau from Interlaken.

52078.q: Which large glacier begins at the Jungfrau?
52078.e: The Aletsch Glacier is the largest glacier in the Alps. It begins in the Jungfrau area.
52078.m: The Aletsch Glacier begins at the Jungfrau.

52079.q: What does the German name “Jungfrau” mean?
52079.e: Jungfrau is an old word for a young, unmarried woman, a maiden.
52079.m: The Jungfrau mountain is named after a young woman.

52080.q: What is the famous, very steep face of the Eiger called?
52080.e: The Eiger North Face is one of the best-known and most difficult rock faces in the Alps.
52080.m: The Eiger North Face is very steep and famous.

52081.q: About how high is the Eiger?
52081.e: The Eiger is about 3967 metres high.
52081.m: The Eiger is just under 4000 metres high.

52082.q: Which village lies below the Eiger?
52082.e: Grindelwald lies right below the North Face of the Eiger.

52083.q: In which canton is the Eiger?
52083.e: The Eiger is in the canton of Bern, in the Bernese Oberland.
52083.m: The Eiger is in the canton of Bern.

52084.q: Which railway runs in a tunnel through the Eiger?
52084.e: The Jungfrau Railway runs through a long tunnel in the Eiger and the Mönch up to the Jungfraujoch.
52084.m: The Jungfrau Railway runs through the Eiger.

52085.q: Where does the Jungfrau Railway go through the tunnel in the Eiger?
52085.e: The Jungfrau Railway runs through the Eiger and the Mönch up to the Jungfraujoch. That is where the highest railway station in Europe is.
52085.m: The Jungfrau Railway goes up to the Jungfraujoch.

52086.q: What is the cable car that has run from Grindelwald to the Eiger Glacier since 2020 called?
52086.e: The Eiger Express opened in December 2020. It takes visitors quickly from Grindelwald up to Eiger Glacier station.
52086.m: The Eiger Express goes from Grindelwald up to the Eiger Glacier.

52087.q: In which year did a person first stand on top of the Eiger?
52087.e: In 1858, Charles Barrington and two mountain guides were the first to reach the summit.
52087.m: The Eiger was first climbed in 1858.

52088.q: Which mountain stands between the Eiger and the Jungfrau?
52088.e: In the row Eiger, Mönch, Jungfrau, the Mönch stands in the middle.
52088.m: The Mönch stands between the Eiger and the Jungfrau.

52089.e: The Mönch is over 4100 metres high. That is why it counts as a four-thousander.
52089.m: The Mönch is higher than 4000 metres.

52090.q: Where do many climbers set off for the Mönch from?
52090.e: The train takes you high up to the Jungfraujoch. From there it is not far to the Mönch.
52090.m: Many people climb the Mönch from the Jungfraujoch.

52091.q: What covers the summit of the Mönch all year round?
52091.e: The Mönch is over 4000 metres high. It is always cold that high up, so snow and ice stay all year round.
52091.m: There is snow on the Mönch all year round.

52092.q: What is a monk (in German “Mönch”), after which the mountain is named?
a: A man who lives in a monastery
A farmer on an alpine pasture
52092.e: A monk is a man who lives and prays in a monastery.
52092.m: A monk lives in a monastery.

52093.q: In which region is the Mönch?
52093.e: The Mönch is part of the famous mountain chain in the Bernese Oberland.
52093.m: The Mönch is in the Bernese Oberland.

52094.q: Which of the three neighbouring mountains is the lowest: Eiger, Mönch or Jungfrau?
a: They are all the same height
52094.e: The Eiger is a little lower than its two neighbours, the Mönch and the Jungfrau.
52094.m: Of the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau, the Eiger is the lowest.

52095.q: Which three mountains form the famous trio in the Bernese Oberland?
52095.e: The Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau stand side by side above Grindelwald and Lauterbrunnen. Together they are called the trio (Dreigestirn).
52095.m: The Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau are the famous trio.

52096.q: Which village lies at the foot of the Titlis?
52096.e: Engelberg is the village below the Titlis. The cable cars up the mountain start from there.
52096.m: Engelberg lies at the foot of the Titlis.

52097.q: What is special about the “Rotair” cable car on the Titlis?
52097.e: The Rotair cabin turns all the way round once during the ride. That way you can see in every direction.
52097.m: The Rotair cable car on the Titlis rotates.

52098.q: About how high is the Titlis?
52098.e: The Titlis is about 3238 metres high.
52098.m: The Titlis is over 3000 metres high.

52099.q: What can visitors see in the glacier ice on the Titlis?
52099.e: On the Titlis, a path leads into a cave in the glacier ice. The walls and ceiling are made of blue ice.
52099.m: There is a cave in the glacier on the Titlis.

52100.e: The Titlis Cliff Walk is a suspension bridge high above a sheer drop. It is said to be one of the highest in Europe.
52100.m: The Titlis Cliff Walk is a suspension bridge.

52101.q: Between which two cantons does the border run over the summit of the Titlis?
52101.e: The border between the cantons of Obwalden and Bern runs over the Titlis.
52101.m: The Titlis lies between Obwalden and Bern.

52102.q: What lies on top of the Titlis even in summer?
52102.e: There is a glacier on top of the Titlis. That is why there is snow and ice there all year round.
52102.m: There is snow and ice on the Titlis all year round.

52103.q: In which region of Switzerland is the Titlis?
52103.e: The Titlis stands near Engelberg in the canton of Obwalden. That is part of Central Switzerland.
52103.m: The Titlis is a well-known mountain in Central Switzerland.

52104.q: In which canton is Piz Bernina?
52104.e: Piz Bernina is in the canton of the Grisons, in the south of the Engadine.
52104.m: Piz Bernina is in the Grisons.

52105.q: What is Piz Bernina for the canton of the Grisons?
52105.e: At over 4000 metres, Piz Bernina is the highest mountain in the Grisons.
52105.m: Piz Bernina is the highest mountain in the Grisons.

52106.q: Which four-thousander stands in eastern Switzerland, far away from all the others?
52106.e: Piz Bernina is the only four-thousander in the Eastern Alps. All the others stand further west.
52106.m: Piz Bernina is the easternmost four-thousander in the Alps.

52107.q: In which valley is the Piz Bernina area?
52107.e: Piz Bernina rises above the Upper Engadine near Pontresina.
52107.m: Piz Bernina rises above the Engadine.

52108.q: What is the narrow, white snow ridge that leads up Piz Bernina called?
52108.e: The Biancograt is a long, narrow ridge of snow. It is often called the “stairway to heaven”.
52108.m: The Biancograt leads up Piz Bernina.

52109.q: What does the word “Piz” in the name Piz Bernina mean?
52109.e: “Piz” is the Romansh word for a mountain peak.

52110.q: Which large glacier flows down into the valley from Piz Bernina?
52110.e: The Morteratsch Glacier comes from the Bernina massif and reaches far down into the valley.
52110.m: The Morteratsch Glacier comes from the Bernina.

52111.q: Besides German, which language is often spoken in the Piz Bernina area?
52111.e: Many people in the Engadine speak Romansh. That is why many mountains there have names like “Piz”.
52111.m: Romansh is often spoken in the Engadine.

52112.q: In which mountain range is the Säntis?
52112.e: The Säntis is the highest peak in the Alpstein in eastern Switzerland.
52112.m: The Säntis is the highest mountain in the Alpstein.

52113.q: About how high is the Säntis?
52113.e: The Säntis is about 2502 metres high.
52113.m: The Säntis is about 2500 metres high.

52114.q: In which region of Switzerland is the Säntis?
52114.e: The Säntis is in eastern Switzerland, near the Appenzell region.
52114.m: The Säntis is in eastern Switzerland.

52115.q: Which cantons meet at the summit of the Säntis?
52115.e: The cantons of Appenzell Ausserrhoden, Appenzell Innerrhoden and St Gallen meet on the Säntis.
52115.m: Appenzell and St Gallen meet on the Säntis.

52116.q: What stands on the Säntis and measures wind, snow and cold?
52116.e: A weather station on the Säntis has been measuring wind, snow and temperature for over 100 years.
52116.m: There is a weather station on the Säntis.

52117.q: How can you get up the Säntis without hiking?
52117.e: An aerial cable car runs from the Schwägalp up the Säntis.
52117.m: An aerial cable car goes up the Säntis.

52118.q: From which place does the cable car up the Säntis start?
52118.e: The valley station of the Säntis cable car is on the Schwägalp.
52118.m: The Säntis cable car starts on the Schwägalp.

52119.q: What can you see well from the Säntis on clear days?
52119.e: The Säntis is not far from Lake Constance. That is why you can see the lake well from the summit.
52119.m: You can see Lake Constance from the Säntis.

52120.q: What stands as a tall tower on the Säntis?
52120.e: A tall transmitter tower stands on the Säntis. It sends radio and television signals across the country.
52120.m: A tall transmitter tower stands on the Säntis.

52121.q: On which lake does the Niesen stand?
52121.e: The Niesen rises on the southern shore of Lake Thun.
52121.m: The Niesen stands by Lake Thun.

52122.q: What does the Niesen look like from far away?
52122.e: The Niesen has evenly steep sides. That is why it is often called the “Swiss pyramid”.
52122.m: The Niesen looks like a pyramid.

52123.q: About how high is the Niesen?
52123.e: The Niesen is about 2362 metres high.
52123.m: The Niesen is about 2360 metres high.

52124.q: Which kind of railway goes up the Niesen?
52124.e: The Niesen railway is a funicular. Its cars run on rails and are pulled up the steep slope by a cable.
52124.m: A funicular goes up the Niesen.

52125.q: What is the staircase next to the Niesen railway famous for?
a: It has a huge number of steps
It is made entirely of glass
It is the oldest staircase in Switzerland
52125.e: A staircase with over 11,000 steps leads up next to the Niesen railway. It is said to be one of the longest staircases in the world.
52125.m: There is a very long staircase next to the Niesen railway.

52126.q: In which canton is the Niesen?
52126.e: The Niesen stands by Lake Thun in the canton of Bern.
52126.m: The Niesen is in the canton of Bern.

52127.q: When are runners allowed to race up the Niesen staircase?
a: Once a year in a race
52127.e: The staircase was built for railway maintenance. A stair race takes place on it only once a year.
52127.m: The Niesen staircase is only open for the yearly race.

52128.q: What is the area around Thun, Interlaken and the Niesen called?
52128.e: The Niesen lies in the Bernese Oberland, the mountain region south of Thun.
52128.m: The Niesen is part of the Bernese Oberland.

52129.e: A four-thousander is a mountain whose summit is more than 4000 metres above sea level.
52129.m: A four-thousander is higher than 4000 metres.

52130.q: In which canton are most of Switzerland's four-thousanders?
52130.e: By far most of Switzerland's four-thousanders are in the canton of Valais.

52131.q: Which of these mountains is a four-thousander?
52131.e: The Matterhorn is about 4478 metres high, which is well over 4000 metres.

52132.q: Which of these mountains is NOT a four-thousander?
52132.e: The Titlis is over 3000 metres high, but it does not reach 4000 metres.
52132.m: The Titlis is not a four-thousander.

52133.q: Roughly how many four-thousanders are there in Switzerland?
52133.e: Depending on how you count, Switzerland has about 40 to 50 peaks over 4000 metres.

52134.q: What almost always lies on the four-thousanders, even in summer?
52134.e: It is very cold that high up. That is why snow and ice stay all year round.
52134.m: There is snow on four-thousanders all year round.

52135.q: Why is it harder to breathe on a four-thousander?
52135.e: The higher you climb, the thinner the air becomes. You get less oxygen with every breath.
52135.m: The air is thin on high mountains.

52136.q: Who takes visitors safely up a four-thousander?
52136.e: Mountain guides know the routes, the weather and the dangers on the mountain.
52136.m: A mountain guide takes visitors safely to the summit.

52137.q: What do climbers need on their boots on a glacier?
52137.e: Crampons have sharp spikes. With them you do not slip on ice.
52137.m: With crampons you do not slip on the ice.

52138.q: What does a summit cross mark?
a: The way down to the valley
52138.e: The summit cross usually stands exactly on the highest point of a mountain.
52138.m: The summit cross marks the highest point.

52139.q: Which book do climbers often sign at the summit cross?
52139.e: There is often a summit book in a box near the summit cross. You write your name and the date in it.
52139.m: You write your name in the summit book.

52140.q: What material are many summit crosses made of?
52140.e: Summit crosses have to withstand wind, snow and lightning. That is why they are made of sturdy materials.
52140.m: Summit crosses are usually made of wood or metal.

52141.q: Which religion does the symbol of the summit cross come from?
52141.e: The cross is the symbol of Christianity. In the past it was put up as a sign of faith.
52141.m: The cross is a symbol of Christianity.

52142.q: What do many hikers do when they reach the summit cross?
52142.e: At the summit cross, many people are happy to have reached their goal and take a photo as a souvenir.
52142.m: People like to take a souvenir photo at the summit cross.

52143.q: Why is a summit cross dangerous in a thunderstorm?
52143.e: A summit cross stands high and in the open, and is often made of metal. That is why lightning easily strikes there.
52143.m: In a thunderstorm, keep away from the summit cross.

52144.q: What is the traditional German greeting climbers use when they reach the top?
52144.e: “Berg Heil” is the old greeting climbers use to congratulate each other on the summit. Skiers say “Ski Heil” and anglers say “Petri Heil”.
52144.m: On the summit, German-speaking climbers say “Berg Heil”.

a: The highest railway station in Europe
The largest indoor pool in Europe
52145.e: No other railway station in Europe is as high as Jungfraujoch station.
52145.m: The highest railway station in Europe is on the Jungfraujoch.

52146.q: At about what height is Jungfraujoch station?
52146.e: Jungfraujoch station lies at about 3454 metres above sea level.
52146.m: Jungfraujoch station is almost 3500 metres high.

52147.q: Which nickname belongs to the Jungfraujoch?
52147.e: The Jungfraujoch is promoted with the English name “Top of Europe”.
52147.m: The Jungfraujoch is also called the “Top of Europe”.

52148.q: What is the domed building on the Jungfraujoch, from which you can see far, called?
52148.e: The Sphinx is a research station with a viewing terrace on a rock at the Jungfraujoch.
52148.m: The Sphinx stands on the Jungfraujoch.

52149.q: What can visitors see in the ice on the Jungfraujoch?
52149.e: Passages and ice sculptures have been carved into the glacier ice. This is called the Ice Palace.
52149.m: There is an Ice Palace on the Jungfraujoch.

52150.q: When was the Jungfrau Railway up to the Jungfraujoch completed?
52150.e: After about 16 years of building work, the Jungfrau Railway reached the Jungfraujoch in 1912.
52150.m: The Jungfrau Railway has run to the Jungfraujoch since 1912.

52151.q: From which station does the Jungfrau Railway start for the Jungfraujoch?
52151.e: The Jungfrau Railway starts at Kleine Scheidegg and then climbs through the tunnel.
52151.m: The Jungfrau Railway starts at Kleine Scheidegg.

52152.q: What is a “Joch” in the mountains?
52152.e: A Joch is a lower point between two mountains, a saddle. The Jungfraujoch lies between the Mönch and the Jungfrau.
52152.m: A Joch is a saddle between two peaks.

52153.q: Which lake is the largest lake in Switzerland?
52153.e: Lake Geneva covers about 580 km². No other lake in Switzerland is so big.
52153.m: Lake Geneva is the largest lake in Switzerland.

52154.q: Which neighbouring country does Switzerland share Lake Geneva with?
52154.e: Most of the southern shore of Lake Geneva belongs to France. About six tenths of the lake belong to Switzerland.
52154.m: Lake Geneva lies in Switzerland and France.

52155.q: About how deep is Lake Geneva at its deepest point?
52155.e: The deepest point of Lake Geneva is off Lausanne. There it is about 310 metres deep.
52155.m: Lake Geneva is up to 310 metres deep.

52156.q: Roughly what shape is Lake Geneva?
52156.e: The northern shore of Lake Geneva forms a long curve. That is why the lake looks like a crescent moon on the map.
52156.m: Lake Geneva is shaped like a crescent moon.

52157.q: Which country does most of the southern shore of Lake Geneva belong to?
52157.e: The northern shore belongs to Switzerland, while most of the southern shore between Geneva and Valais belongs to France. Towns such as Évian and Thonon-les-Bains lie there.
52157.m: France lies on the southern shore of Lake Geneva.

52158.q: Which town on Lake Geneva is known for its big jazz festival?
52158.e: A famous jazz festival takes place in Montreux every summer, right on the lakeshore.
52158.m: Montreux on Lake Geneva is known for its jazz festival.

52159.q: Which river flows through Lake Geneva?
52159.e: The Rhone flows into Lake Geneva near Villeneuve and leaves it again in Geneva.
52159.m: The Rhone flows through Lake Geneva.

52160.q: Which city with the Olympic Museum lies on Lake Geneva?
52160.e: Lausanne lies on the northern shore of Lake Geneva. The Olympic Museum stands there right by the lake.
52160.m: Lausanne is the Olympic Capital on Lake Geneva.

52161.q: What grows in especially large amounts on the steep slopes by Lake Geneva?
52161.e: On the northern shore of Lake Geneva there are many terraced vineyards. Grapes grow there.
52161.m: Many grapevines grow by Lake Geneva.

52162.q: Which canton lies on Lake Geneva?
52162.e: The cantons of Geneva, Vaud and Valais lie on the Swiss shore of Lake Geneva. Vaud has the longest stretch of shore.
52162.m: Vaud has the longest shore on Lake Geneva.

52163.q: Which little town on the southern shore of Lake Neuchâtel has “on the lake” in its name?
52163.e: Estavayer-le-Lac lies in the canton of Fribourg on the southern shore. In French, “le Lac” means “the lake”.

52164.q: Which town lies on the northern shore of Lake Neuchâtel?
52164.e: The town of Neuchâtel lies on the northern shore and gives the lake its name.
52164.m: The town of Neuchâtel gives Lake Neuchâtel its name.

52165.q: Roughly how big is Lake Neuchâtel?
52165.e: Lake Neuchâtel has an area of about 218 square kilometres. That makes it a very large lake.
52165.m: Lake Neuchâtel covers about 218 square kilometres.

52166.q: Which river from the Val de Travers flows into Lake Neuchâtel?
52166.e: The Areuse flows through the Val de Travers in the Jura. It is one of the most important rivers flowing into Lake Neuchâtel.
52166.m: The Areuse flows into Lake Neuchâtel.

52167.q: Which mountain range rises on the northern shore of Lake Neuchâtel?
52167.e: Behind the northern shore, the hills and mountains of the Jura rise up.
52167.m: The Jura begins at Lake Neuchâtel.

52168.q: How many cantons border Lake Neuchâtel?
52168.e: Lake Neuchâtel borders the cantons of Neuchâtel, Vaud, Fribourg and Bern.

52169.q: Through which canal does the water flow from Lake Neuchâtel into Lake Biel?
52169.e: The outflow of Lake Neuchâtel is the Zihl. It flows into Lake Biel in the Zihl Canal.
52169.m: The Zihl Canal connects Lake Neuchâtel with Lake Biel.

52170.q: Which is the largest lake that lies entirely in Switzerland?
52170.e: Lake Neuchâtel is the largest lake that belongs entirely to Switzerland. Lake Geneva and Lake Constance are larger, but they also lie in other countries.
52170.m: Lake Neuchâtel is the largest lake lying entirely in Switzerland.

52171.q: How did people live on the shores of Lake Neuchâtel in the Stone Age?
a: In tents made of animal skins
52171.e: Thousands of years ago, people already lived in houses on stilts by Lake Neuchâtel. These are called pile dwellings. Some of the sites are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
52171.m: There were pile dwellings by Lake Neuchâtel in the Stone Age.

52172.q: Which little town with a castle lies on the south-western shore of Lake Biel?
52172.e: Erlach lies at the foot of the Jolimont on Lake Biel. A castle stands above the small Old Town.
52172.m: Erlach is a little castle town on Lake Biel.

52173.q: What is the well-known peninsula in Lake Biel that used to be an island called?
52173.e: St Peter's Island lies in the south-west of Lake Biel. Today it is connected to the shore by a narrow strip of land.
52173.m: St Peter's Island lies in Lake Biel.

52174.q: Which famous thinker lived on St Peter's Island for a few weeks in the 18th century?
52174.e: The philosopher Jean-Jacques Rousseau spent a few weeks on the island in 1765. He later wrote that he had been very happy there.
52174.m: Rousseau once lived on St Peter's Island.

52175.q: Why is St Peter's Island in Lake Biel no longer a real island today?
a: A landslide filled in the lake.
The lake dried up in summer.
52175.e: During the first Jura water correction, the lake level was lowered by about 2.5 metres. This exposed a strip of land reaching to the island.
52175.m: Since the lake level dropped, St Peter's Island has been a peninsula.

52176.q: Which river is diverted into Lake Biel through the Hagneck Canal?
52176.e: Since the Jura water correction, the Aare has flowed through the Hagneck Canal into Lake Biel. That way it leaves its mud in the lake.
52176.m: The Aare flows through the Hagneck Canal into Lake Biel.

52177.q: What grows on the sunny slopes by Lake Biel?
52177.e: Many vines grow on the steep, sunny slopes above Lake Biel. The grapes are made into wine.
52177.m: Vines for wine grow by Lake Biel.

52178.q: What is Lake Biel called in French?
52178.e: Biel is called Bienne in French. That is why the lake is called “Lac de Bienne”.
52178.m: In French, Lake Biel is called Lac de Bienne.

52179.q: In which canton is almost all of Lake Biel?
52179.e: Almost all of Lake Biel belongs to the canton of Bern. Only a small part in the west belongs to Neuchâtel.
52179.m: Lake Biel lies almost entirely in the canton of Bern.

52180.q: Which wine-growing village with a wine museum lies on Lake Biel?
52180.e: Ligerz lies among vineyards on the northern shore of Lake Biel. There is a museum about wine growing there.
52180.m: Ligerz is a wine-growing village on Lake Biel.

52181.q: About how deep is Lake Thun at its deepest point?
52181.e: Lake Thun is up to 217 metres deep.
52181.m: Lake Thun is over 200 metres deep.

52182.q: What stands on a hill above the Old Town in the town of Thun?
52182.e: High above the Old Town of Thun stands a castle with a big tower. The town lies at the end of Lake Thun.
52182.m: In Thun, a castle stands above the Old Town.

52183.q: Which pyramid-shaped mountain rises above Lake Thun near Spiez?
52183.e: The Niesen looks like a big pyramid. A funicular runs up to its summit.
52183.m: The Niesen is the pyramid mountain by Lake Thun.

52184.q: Which caves can you visit on the northern shore of Lake Thun?
52184.e: The St Beatus Caves lie high above the northern shore of Lake Thun. Paths lead far into the mountain.
52184.m: The St Beatus Caves are by Lake Thun.

52185.q: In which canton is Lake Thun?
52185.e: Lake Thun lies entirely in the canton of Bern. It is the largest Swiss lake that belongs to just one canton.
52185.m: Lake Thun lies entirely in the canton of Bern.

52186.q: Which place lies between Lake Thun and Lake Brienz?
52186.e: Interlaken lies on a plain between two lakes. The name means “between the lakes”.
52186.m: Interlaken lies between Lake Thun and Lake Brienz.

52187.q: Which river was diverted into Lake Thun more than 300 years ago?
52187.e: The Kander often caused floods in the past. That is why it was diverted into Lake Thun between 1712 and 1714.
52187.m: The Kander has flowed into Lake Thun for more than 300 years.

52188.q: What kind of ship is the “Blümlisalp” on Lake Thun?
52188.e: The “Blümlisalp” is a historic steamship with big paddle wheels. It still sails across the lake in summer today.
52188.m: The Blümlisalp is a paddle steamer on Lake Thun.

52189.q: Which castle on Lake Thun has a little turret standing in the water?
52189.e: Oberhofen Castle stands on the northern shore of Lake Thun. Its little tower stands right in the water.
52189.m: Oberhofen Castle has a turret in Lake Thun.

52190.q: In which village on Lake Brienz is woodcarving especially famous?
52190.e: Brienz has had many woodcarvers for a long time, and a school for wood sculpture.
52190.m: Brienz is the village of woodcarvers.

52191.q: What are the waterfalls that plunge into Lake Brienz in 14 steps called?
52191.e: The Giessbach Falls plunge in 14 steps down into Lake Brienz on the southern shore. An old grand hotel stands next to them.
52191.m: The Giessbach Falls plunge into Lake Brienz.

52192.q: What colour is the water of Lake Brienz often?
52192.e: Glacier streams bring fine rock dust into the lake. This makes the water glow turquoise green.
52192.m: Lake Brienz often glows turquoise green.

52193.q: What is the water in Lake Brienz like?
52193.e: The water of Lake Brienz contains few nutrients. It is considered one of the cleanest lakes in Switzerland.
52193.m: Lake Brienz is one of the cleanest lakes in Switzerland.

52194.q: Which river from the Lauterbrunnen and Grindelwald valleys flows into Lake Brienz?
52194.e: The Lütschine collects the water from the Lauterbrunnen and Grindelwald valleys. It flows into Lake Brienz at Bönigen.
52194.m: The Lütschine flows into Lake Brienz.

52195.q: Which of these lakes lies highest above sea level?
52195.e: Lake Brienz lies at about 564 metres above sea level, a few metres higher than Lake Thun. That is why the water flows from Lake Brienz to Lake Thun.
52195.m: Lake Brienz lies higher than Lake Thun.

52196.q: About how deep is Lake Brienz at its deepest point?
52196.e: Lake Brienz is up to 260 metres deep. Its steep shores also drop away steeply under the water.
52196.m: Lake Brienz is up to 260 metres deep.

52197.q: Which mountain does a steam cog railway run up from Brienz?
52197.e: The Brienz Rothorn Railway runs with steam locomotives from Brienz up the Brienzer Rothorn. From the top you can see far across the lake.
52197.m: A steam railway runs from Brienz up the Rothorn.

52198.q: About how long is Lake Brienz?
52198.e: Lake Brienz is about 14 kilometres long and just under 3 kilometres wide.
52198.m: Lake Brienz is about 14 kilometres long.

52199.q: Which two cantons border Lake Walen?
52199.e: Most of Lake Walen belongs to St Gallen, and the western end also to Glarus.
52199.m: Lake Walen lies in St Gallen and Glarus.

52200.q: Which mountain chain with seven peaks rises steeply above the northern shore of Lake Walen?
52200.e: The Churfirsten are a row of seven peaks. They drop almost vertically down to Lake Walen.
52200.m: The seven Churfirsten stand above Lake Walen.

52201.q: Which village on Lake Walen has no road and can only be reached by boat or on foot?
52201.e: Quinten lies on the steep northern shore. It is car-free, and you can only get there by boat or on a long hike.
52201.m: Quinten on Lake Walen is a car-free village.

52202.q: Which canal carries the water from Lake Walen into Lake Zurich?
52202.e: The Linth flows through Lake Walen. After that, the Linth Canal carries it on into Lake Zurich.
52202.m: The Linth Canal connects Lake Walen with Lake Zurich.

52203.q: Which town lies at the eastern end of Lake Walen?
52203.e: Walenstadt lies at the eastern end of the lake. Weesen lies at the other end in the west.
52203.m: Walenstadt lies at the eastern end of Lake Walen.

52204.q: How do the motorway and the railway pass Lake Walen?
a: Through tunnels on the southern shore
Over a bridge in the middle of the lake
52204.e: On the steep southern shore, the motorway and the railway run through many tunnels and galleries.
52204.m: The motorway and the railway run through tunnels on the southern shore of Lake Walen.

52205.q: Roughly how big is Lake Walen?
52205.e: Lake Walen has an area of about 24 square kilometres.
52205.m: Lake Walen covers about 24 square kilometres.

52206.q: In which part of Switzerland is Lake Walen?
52206.e: Lake Walen lies between Lake Zurich and the Sarganserland in eastern Switzerland.
52206.m: Lake Walen is in eastern Switzerland.

52207.q: Which high waterfalls plunge into Lake Walen near Betlis on the northern shore?
52207.e: The Seerenbach Falls are near Betlis above Lake Walen. They are among the highest waterfalls in Switzerland.
52207.m: The Seerenbach Falls plunge down towards Lake Walen.

52208.q: Which little town with a town wall you can walk along lies on Lake Murten?
52208.e: Murten has a well-preserved town wall from the Middle Ages. You can walk along it and look out over the lake.
52208.m: Murten has an old town wall that you can walk on.

52209.q: In which year did the Battle of Murten take place?
52209.e: The Battle of Murten was in 1476. The Swiss Confederates won it.
52209.m: The Battle of Murten was in 1476.

52210.q: Which ruler did the Swiss Confederates fight against in the Battle of Murten?
52210.e: Charles the Bold was Duke of Burgundy. His army was defeated by the Swiss Confederates at Murten.
52210.m: At Murten, the Swiss Confederates defeated Charles the Bold.

52211.q: What is Lake Murten called in French?
52211.e: The little town of Murten is called Morat in French. That is why the lake is called “Lac de Morat”.
52211.m: In French, Lake Murten is called Lac de Morat.

52212.q: Which hill with vineyards lies on the northern shore of Lake Murten?
52212.e: Mont Vully lies between Lake Murten and Lake Neuchâtel. Many vines grow on its slope facing Lake Murten.
52212.m: Wine grows on Mont Vully above Lake Murten.

52213.e: Lake Murten lies between the cantons of Fribourg and Vaud.
52213.m: Lake Murten lies in Fribourg and Vaud.

52214.q: Which river flows through Lake Murten?
52214.e: The Broye flows into Lake Murten. Its water then flows on through the Broye Canal into Lake Neuchâtel.
52214.m: The Broye flows through Lake Murten.

52215.q: Which is the smallest of the three large lakes at the foot of the Jura?
52215.e: Lake Murten covers about 23 km². It is smaller than Lake Neuchâtel and Lake Biel.
52215.m: Lake Murten is the smallest of the three Jura foothill lakes.

52216.q: About how deep is Lake Murten at its deepest point?
52216.e: Lake Murten is at most about 45 metres deep. So it is a rather shallow lake.
52216.m: Lake Murten is at most about 45 metres deep.

52217.q: What kind of lake is the Sihlsee?
52217.e: The Sihlsee was created when a dam was built and the valley was filled with water. So it was made by people.
52217.m: The Sihlsee is an artificial reservoir.

52218.q: What record does the Sihlsee hold?
a: Largest reservoir in Switzerland by area
52218.e: At almost 11 km², no other reservoir in Switzerland covers such a large area.
52218.m: The Sihlsee is the largest reservoir in Switzerland by area.

52219.q: In which canton is the Sihlsee?
52219.e: The Sihlsee lies in the district of Einsiedeln in the canton of Schwyz.
52219.m: The Sihlsee is in the canton of Schwyz.

52220.q: Near which village with a famous abbey does the Sihlsee lie?
52220.e: The Sihlsee lies in the high valley of Einsiedeln. Einsiedeln Abbey is a famous place of pilgrimage.

52221.q: Which river is dammed to form the Sihlsee?
52221.e: The Sihlsee is named after the Sihl. Its water is held back by a dam.
52221.m: The Sihl is dammed to form the Sihlsee.

52222.q: What kind of lake is the Sihlsee near Einsiedeln?
52222.e: For the Sihlsee, a valley was closed off with a dam and flooded in 1937. It is one of the largest reservoirs in Switzerland.

52223.q: What is the water of the Sihlsee mainly used for?
52223.e: The water drives the Etzelwerk. This power station supplies railway electricity for the SBB, the Swiss Federal Railways.
52223.m: The Sihlsee supplies electricity for SBB trains.

52224.q: About how deep is the Sihlsee at its deepest point?
52224.e: The Sihlsee is big, but only up to about 23 metres deep. It fills a shallow high valley.
52224.m: The Sihlsee is big but not very deep.

52225.q: How can cars cross the Sihlsee?
52225.e: When the Sihlsee was built, two long bridges called viaducts were built across the lake.

52226.q: Above which village does Lake Oeschinen lie?
52226.e: Lake Oeschinen lies in a side valley above Kandersteg.

52227.q: In which region is Lake Oeschinen?
52227.e: Kandersteg and Lake Oeschinen are part of the Bernese Oberland in the canton of Bern.
52227.m: Lake Oeschinen is in the Bernese Oberland.

52228.q: At about what height does Lake Oeschinen lie?
52228.e: The surface of the water lies at about 1578 metres above sea level.
52228.m: Lake Oeschinen lies almost 1600 metres above sea level.

a: By a stream digging a hole
52229.e: Several rockfalls blocked the valley with rocks. Behind them, the water built up into a lake.

52230.q: Which mountain massif with glaciers rises behind Lake Oeschinen?
52230.e: Behind the lake, the Blüemlisalp and other peaks tower over 3000 metres high.
52230.m: The Blüemlisalp stands behind Lake Oeschinen.

52231.q: Which kind of lift takes you comfortably from Kandersteg to near Lake Oeschinen?
52231.e: Since 2008, a gondola has run up from Kandersteg. From the top station it is still about a 25-minute walk to the lake.
52231.m: A gondola goes from Kandersteg towards Lake Oeschinen.

52232.q: Which UNESCO World Heritage Site does Lake Oeschinen belong to?
52232.e: Since 2007, Lake Oeschinen has been part of the extended World Heritage Site Swiss Alps Jungfrau-Aletsch.
52232.m: Lake Oeschinen is part of the Jungfrau-Aletsch World Heritage Site.

52233.q: What can you do on Lake Oeschinen in some winters?
52233.e: In cold winters, Lake Oeschinen freezes over. When the ice is thick enough and there is little snow on it, you can skate on it.
52233.m: In some winters you can skate on Lake Oeschinen.

52234.q: Roughly how big is Lake Oeschinen?
52234.e: Lake Oeschinen covers about 1.1 square kilometres. That is quite big for a mountain lake.
52234.m: Lake Oeschinen covers about one square kilometre.

52236.q: In which canton is the Grande Dixence dam?
52236.e: The Grande Dixence stands in the Val d'Hérémence in the canton of Valais.
52236.m: The Grande Dixence is in Valais.

52237.q: What lies behind the Grande Dixence dam?
52237.e: Behind the wall, the water builds up into the Lac des Dix, a large reservoir.
52237.m: A large reservoir lies behind the Grande Dixence.

52238.q: Which world record does the Grande Dixence hold?
a: Highest gravity dam in the world
52238.e: A gravity dam holds back the water with its enormous weight. No other dam of this kind is as high.
52238.m: The Grande Dixence is the highest gravity dam in the world.

52239.q: About how long is the Lac des Dix behind the Grande Dixence?
52239.e: The reservoir behind the dam is about 5 kilometres long.
52239.m: The Lac des Dix is about 5 kilometres long.

52240.q: Where does most of the water in the Lac des Dix come from?
52240.e: In summer, the glaciers around the lake melt. The meltwater is collected and channelled into the reservoir.
52240.m: The Lac des Dix is filled with glacier water.

52241.q: What is the Grande Dixence dam built of?
52241.e: Huge amounts of concrete were used to build the wall. That is why it is very heavy and holds back the water.
52241.m: The Grande Dixence is built of concrete.

52242.q: Where is the reservoir of the Grande Dixence?
a: In the middle of a city
52242.e: The Lac des Dix lies in Valais at over 2300 metres above sea level, high up in the mountains.
52242.m: The Lac des Dix lies high up in the mountains.

52243.q: Which reservoir in Switzerland can store the most water?
52243.e: The lake behind the Grande Dixence holds about 400 million cubic metres of water. That is more than any other Swiss reservoir.
52243.m: The Lac des Dix stores the most water of all Swiss reservoirs.

52244.q: What is the water like in most mountain lakes?
52244.e: Mountain lakes lie high up, where it is cool. Meltwater from snow and glaciers often flows into them.
52244.m: The water in mountain lakes is usually very cold.

52245.q: What happens to many mountain lakes in winter?
52245.e: It is very cold in the mountains in winter. That is why a thick layer of ice forms on many mountain lakes.
52245.m: Many mountain lakes freeze over in winter.

52246.q: Which mountain lake lies in the Alpstein below the Ebenalp?
52246.e: The Seealpsee lies in the canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden. You can reach it on foot from Wasserauen.
52246.m: The Seealpsee lies in the Alpstein.

52247.q: Which mountain lake lies near the First viewpoint above Grindelwald?
52247.e: The Bachalpsee lies at about 2265 metres above sea level. The mountains of the Bernese Oberland are reflected in its water.

52248.q: Which turquoise lake lies in the forest near Flims in the Grisons?
52248.e: The Caumasee is fed by underground springs. Its water glows turquoise between the trees.
52248.m: The Caumasee near Flims glows turquoise.

52249.q: Which fish often lives in mountain lakes?
52249.e: Trout like cold, clean water. That is why they like living in mountain lakes. The other fish live in the sea.
52249.m: Trout often live in mountain lakes.

52250.q: Where does a lot of the water in mountain lakes come from in spring?
52250.e: In spring, the snow in the mountains melts. The meltwater flows into the mountain lakes.
52250.m: Meltwater fills the mountain lakes in spring.

52251.q: What formed many mountain lakes in the Alps a long time ago?
52251.e: In the past, thick glaciers lay in the Alps. They ground hollows into the rock. When the ice melted, the hollows filled with water.

52252.q: Which mountain lake with a spooky name lies on the Grimsel Pass?
52252.e: The Totensee lies right at the top of the Grimsel Pass between Bern and Valais.
52252.m: The Totensee lies on the Grimsel Pass.

52253.q: What are the two source rivers of the Rhine called?
52253.e: The Vorderrhein (Front Rhine) and the Hinterrhein (Rear Rhine) flow together in the Grisons. From there on, the river is simply called the Rhine.
52253.m: The Vorderrhein and the Hinterrhein together form the Rhine.

52254.q: From which small mountain lake does the Vorderrhein flow?
52254.e: Lake Toma lies near the Oberalp Pass. It is considered the source of the Vorderrhein.
52254.m: Lake Toma near the Oberalp Pass is the source of the Vorderrhein.

52255.q: Through which large lake does the Rhine flow in the east of Switzerland?
52255.e: The Rhine flows into Lake Constance and comes out again at Stein am Rhein. Switzerland, Germany and Austria border Lake Constance.
52255.m: The Rhine flows through Lake Constance.

52256.q: Near which place do the Vorderrhein and the Hinterrhein flow together?
52256.e: The two source rivers meet at Reichenau near Chur. From there on, the river is called the Rhine.
52256.m: At Reichenau, two rivers become the Rhine.

52257.q: In which Swiss city does the Rhine leave Switzerland?
52257.e: The Rhine flows out of Switzerland at Basel. After that, it flows on north between Germany and France.
52257.m: The Rhine leaves Switzerland at Basel.

52258.q: Where in Switzerland is there a port for large Rhine ships?
52258.e: Basel has the Rhine ports. From there, cargo ships travel on the Rhine all the way to the sea.
52258.m: Basel has a port on the Rhine.

52259.q: Which cantonal capital in the Grisons lies in the Rhine valley?
52259.e: Chur is the capital of the Grisons. The town lies in the Rhine valley close to the Rhine.
52259.m: Chur lies in the Rhine valley.

52260.q: Which river forms the border between the canton of St Gallen and Austria?
52260.e: In the St Gallen Rhine valley, the Rhine flows between Switzerland and Austria. There it is the border river.
52260.m: In the Rhine valley, the Rhine separates Switzerland from Austria.

52261.q: Which river is the longest river that flows entirely within Switzerland?
52261.e: The Aare is about 290 kilometres long. From beginning to end it flows only through Switzerland.
52261.m: The Aare is the longest river entirely in Switzerland.

52262.e: The Aare comes from the Oberaar Glacier and the Unteraar Glacier. These lie in the Grimsel area in the Bernese Alps.
52262.m: The Aare rises near the Grimsel.

52263.q: What do many people in Bern do in the Aare in summer?
52263.e: In summer, many people in Bern let themselves drift down the river. This is called the Aareschwumm.
52263.m: In summer, many people in Bern swim in the Aare.

52264.q: Through which two lakes in the Bernese Oberland does the Aare flow?
52264.e: The Aare first flows into Lake Brienz. At Interlaken it flows on into Lake Thun.
52264.m: The Aare flows through Lake Brienz and Lake Thun.

52265.q: Which canton gets its name from the Aare?
52265.e: The name Aargau roughly means “land on the Aare”. The Aare flows right through this canton.
52265.m: The canton of Aargau is named after the Aare.

52266.q: Which of these towns lies on the Aare?
52266.e: The Aare flows right through the Old Town of Solothurn. Several bridges cross the river there.

52267.q: What colour is the water of the Aare in Bern often in summer?
52267.e: Some of the Aare's water comes from glaciers. Tiny particles of rock often make the water turquoise.
52267.m: The Aare water often glows turquoise in summer.

52268.q: Where do the Aare, Reuss and Limmat flow together?
52268.e: Near Brugg in the canton of Aargau, the three rivers meet one after the other. This area is called the “moated castle of Switzerland”.
52268.m: The Aare, Reuss and Limmat meet near Brugg.

52269.q: Which glacier does the Rhone come from?
52269.e: The Rhone rises at the Rhone Glacier near the Furka Pass. It lies right at the top of the canton of Valais.
52269.m: The Rhone comes from the Rhone Glacier.

52270.q: Through which canton does the Rhone flow before Lake Geneva?
52270.e: The Rhone flows through the whole Rhone valley in Valais. After that it flows into Lake Geneva.

52271.q: Which river flows into the Rhone in Geneva?
52271.e: The Arve comes from the Mont Blanc area in France. In Geneva it flows into the Rhone.
52271.m: The Arve flows into the Rhone in Geneva.

52272.q: In which city does the Rhône leave Lake Geneva?
52272.e: In Geneva the Rhône flows out of the lake. Shortly afterwards it flows into France.
52272.m: The Rhône leaves Lake Geneva in Geneva.

52273.q: Which capital of the canton of Valais lies on the Rhône?
52273.e: Sion is called Sitten in German and is the capital of Valais. The town lies in the Rhône valley.

52274.q: In which direction does the Rhône flow through Valais?
52274.e: The Rhône begins in the east of Valais near the Furka Pass. It then flows west to Lake Geneva.
52274.m: In Valais the Rhône flows from east to west.

52275.q: What is the Rhône called in Upper Valais in the local Swiss German dialect?
52275.e: In German-speaking Upper Valais the Rhône is traditionally called Rotten. In French it is called Rhône.
52275.m: In Upper Valais the Rhône is called Rotten.

52276.q: Why are parts of the Rhône Glacier covered with white sheets in summer?
a: So that hikers can find the way
So that the ice stays clean
So that it gets warmer there
52276.e: The white sheets reflect the sunlight. This makes the ice near the ice grotto melt more slowly.
52276.m: White sheets protect the glacier ice from the sun.

52277.q: Roughly how long is the Inn?
52277.e: The Inn is about 517 kilometres long. Most of it lies in Austria and Germany.
52277.m: The Inn is about 500 kilometres long.

52278.q: Which sea does the water of the Inn end up in?
52278.e: The water of the Inn flows on east through Austria and Germany. Via a great river it finally reaches the Black Sea.
52278.m: The water of the Inn flows into the Black Sea.

52279.q: Which big river does the Inn flow into?
52279.e: The Inn flows through Austria and joins the Danube at Passau. Passau is in Germany.
52279.m: The Inn flows into the Danube.

52280.q: What is the Inn called in Romansh?
52280.e: In Romansh the Inn is called “En”. This is also where the name Engadine comes from.
52280.m: In Romansh the Inn is called En.

52281.q: In which canton does the Inn have its source?
52281.e: The Inn rises at Lake Lunghin high above Maloja in the Upper Engadine. That is in the canton of the Grisons.
52281.m: The Inn has its source in the Grisons.

52282.q: Which of these lakes does the Inn flow through?
52282.e: In the Upper Engadine the Inn flows through Lake Sils, Lake Silvaplana and Lake St Moritz. These lakes lie very high up.
52282.m: The Inn flows through Lake Sils.

52283.q: Which neighbouring country does the Inn flow into when it leaves Switzerland?
52283.e: The Inn leaves Switzerland in the Lower Engadine. After that it flows through Tyrol in Austria.
52283.m: The Inn flows from Switzerland into Austria.

52284.q: Which city in Austria has the Inn in its name?
52284.e: Innsbruck means “bridge over the Inn”. The city is the capital of Tyrol.

52285.q: Which famous holiday resort in the Engadine lies on a lake of the Inn?
52285.e: St Moritz lies on Lake St Moritz. The Inn flows through this lake.
52285.m: St Moritz lies on the Inn.

52286.q: Which valley does the Ticino flow through just after its source?
52286.e: The Bedretto Valley lies at the very top of Ticino. The young Ticino flows through this valley as far as Airolo.
52286.m: The young Ticino flows through the Bedretto Valley.

52287.q: Which language is spoken along the River Ticino in Switzerland?
52287.e: The Ticino flows through the canton of Ticino. Italian is spoken there.
52287.m: Italian is spoken along the Ticino.

52288.q: Which big lake does the Ticino flow into?
52288.e: The Ticino flows into Lake Maggiore on the Magadino plain near Locarno. The lake belongs to Switzerland and Italy.
52288.m: The Ticino flows into Lake Maggiore.

52289.q: Near which pass does the Ticino have its source?
52289.e: The Ticino rises near the Nufenen Pass. The pass lies between Valais and Ticino.
52289.m: The Ticino rises near the Nufenen Pass.

52290.q: Which town with three castles lies on the Ticino?
52290.e: Bellinzona is the capital of Ticino. Its three castles are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
52290.m: Bellinzona with its three castles lies on the Ticino.

52291.q: Which valley does the Ticino flow through after Airolo?
52291.e: From Airolo the Ticino flows south through the Leventina. The Gotthard road and railway also run through this valley.
52291.m: The Ticino flows through the Leventina.

52292.q: In which direction does the Ticino flow?
52292.e: The Ticino comes from the Alps and flows south. That is how it reaches Italy.

52293.q: Which famous wooden bridge in Lucerne crosses the Reuss?
52293.e: The Chapel Bridge is an old covered wooden bridge. It crosses the Reuss in Lucerne and has a water tower.
52293.m: The Chapel Bridge in Lucerne crosses the Reuss.

52294.q: In which canton does the Reuss have its source?
52294.e: The Reuss rises in the Gotthard area in the canton of Uri. It flows through Andermatt and the Reuss valley of Uri.
52294.m: The Reuss rises in the canton of Uri.

52295.q: Which lake does the Reuss flow through?
52295.e: The Reuss flows into Lake Lucerne at Flüelen. In Lucerne it flows out again.
52295.m: The Reuss flows through Lake Lucerne.

52296.q: In which town does the Reuss leave Lake Lucerne?
52296.e: Lucerne lies at the western end of the lake. There the Reuss flows out of the lake and right through the old town.
52296.m: The Reuss leaves Lake Lucerne in Lucerne.

52297.q: What is the famous bridge over the Reuss in the Schöllenen Gorge called?
52297.e: The Devil's Bridge crosses the wild Reuss near Andermatt. An old legend says the Devil built it.
52297.m: The Devil's Bridge crosses the Reuss in the Schöllenen Gorge.

52298.q: Which second old wooden bridge with paintings crosses the Reuss in Lucerne?
52298.e: The Spreuer Bridge is a covered wooden bridge with old paintings. The Lake Bridge and the Reuss Bridge are newer bridges, and the Devil's Bridge is in the Schöllenen Gorge.
52298.m: The Spreuer Bridge crosses the Reuss in Lucerne.

52299.q: Roughly how long is the Reuss?
52299.e: The Reuss is about 164 kilometres long. It is one of the biggest rivers in Switzerland.
52299.m: The Reuss is about 160 kilometres long.

52300.q: Which village on the Gotthard lies on the Reuss?
52300.e: Andermatt lies in the Urseren Valley. The Reuss flows right through this valley.

52301.q: In which direction does the Reuss flow from the Gotthard?
52301.e: The Reuss flows north from the Gotthard to Lake Lucerne. After that it carries on north to the Aare.
52301.m: The Reuss flows north from the Gotthard.

52302.q: Which big city does the Limmat flow through?
52302.e: The Limmat flows right through the old town of Zurich. The Grossmünster and the Fraumünster stand on its banks.

52303.q: Which lake does the Limmat flow out of?
52303.e: The Limmat begins at the lower end of Lake Zurich in Zurich. From there it flows north-west.
52303.m: The Limmat flows out of Lake Zurich.

52304.q: Roughly how long is the Limmat?
52304.e: The Limmat is about 36 kilometres long. It is a rather short river, but it carries a lot of water.
52304.m: The Limmat is a short river of about 35 kilometres.

52305.q: What is the river called that flows into Lake Walen and Lake Zurich before it becomes the Limmat?
52305.e: The Linth comes from the canton of Glarus. The water flows through Lake Walen and Lake Zurich and is then called the Limmat.
52305.m: After Lake Zurich the Linth becomes the Limmat.

52306.q: Which spa town in Aargau lies on the Limmat?
52306.e: The town of Baden lies on the Limmat. It has been known for its warm springs since Roman times.
52306.m: The spa town of Baden lies on the Limmat.

52307.q: Which big church with two towers stands in Zurich close to the Limmat?
52307.e: The Grossmünster stands in Zurich's old town close to the Limmat. Its two towers are a landmark of Zurich.
52307.m: The Grossmünster stands on the Limmat in Zurich.

52308.q: Which smaller river flows into the Limmat in Zurich?
52308.e: The Sihl comes from Lake Sihl. It joins the Limmat at the Platzspitz in Zurich.
52308.m: The Sihl flows into the Limmat in Zurich.

52309.q: Which bigger river does the Limmat flow into?
52309.e: The Limmat flows into the Aare near Brugg. The Reuss and the Aare also meet there.
52309.m: The Limmat flows into the Aare.

52310.q: Which town lies in the Limmat valley between Zurich and Baden?
52310.e: The Limmat flows from Zurich through the Limmat valley to Baden. Places such as Dietikon and Schlieren lie in this valley.
52310.m: Dietikon lies in the Limmat valley.

52311.q: What is the Saane called in French?
52311.e: In the French-speaking part of Switzerland the Saane is called “Sarine”. It flows through areas where German and French are spoken.
52311.m: In French the Saane is called the Sarine.

52312.q: Which bilingual cantonal capital lies on the Saane?
52312.e: Fribourg is called Freiburg in German. Its old town lies in a loop of the Saane.

52313.q: Which language border partly runs along the Saane?
52313.e: In the canton of Fribourg the Saane separates German-speaking and French-speaking areas in some places. In the town of Fribourg both languages are spoken.
52313.m: German and French meet on the Saane.

52314.q: What is the language border often linked with the Saane jokingly called?
52314.e: The “Röstigraben” (rösti ditch) means the border between German-speaking and French-speaking Switzerland. The Saane is seen as a picture of this border.
52314.m: The Röstigraben separates German-speaking and French-speaking Switzerland.

52315.q: Which river does the Saane flow into?
52315.e: The Saane flows north. In the canton of Bern it flows into the Aare.
52315.m: The Saane flows into the Aare.

52316.q: Which reservoir in the Gruyère region does the Saane flow through?
52316.e: The Saane is dammed at Rossens to form Lake Gruyère. In French it is called Lac de la Gruyère.
52316.m: The Saane flows through Lake Gruyère.

52317.q: Which village near Gstaad has almost the same name as the Saane?
52317.e: The Saane flows through Saanen near Gstaad. The village got its name from the river.
52317.m: The village of Saanen is named after the Saane.

52318.q: In which canton does the Saane have its source?
52318.e: The Saane rises at the Sanetschhorn in the canton of Valais. Then it flows north into the Bernese Oberland.

52319.q: Which of these cantons does the Saane not flow through?
52319.e: The Saane flows through Valais, Bern, Vaud and Fribourg. The Grisons lie far to the east.
52319.m: The Saane flows through western Switzerland and Bern.

52320.q: Which canton is named after the Thur?
52320.e: The name Thurgau means “land on the Thur”. The Thur flows right through the canton.
52320.m: Thurgau is named after the Thur.

52321.q: Which valley in the canton of St Gallen does the Thur flow through?
52321.e: The Thur rises in the upper Toggenburg. It flows through places such as Wattwil and Lichtensteig.
52321.m: The Thur flows through the Toggenburg.

52322.q: Which river does the Thur flow into?
52322.e: The Thur flows into the Rhine near Flaach. It is one of the big tributaries of the Rhine.
52322.m: The Thur flows into the Rhine.

52323.q: Near which mountain does the Thur have its source?
52323.e: The Thur rises in the uppermost Toggenburg south of the Säntis. One of its source streams is called the Säntisthur.
52323.m: The Thur rises near the Säntis.

52324.q: Why can the Thur rise very quickly when it rains?
a: Because no lake catches the water
Because it comes from the sea
52324.e: The Thur does not flow through any big lake. That is why its water rises quickly when there is a lot of rain.
52324.m: Without a lake, the Thur rises quickly when it rains.

52325.q: Which town in Thurgau lies on the Thur?
52325.e: The Thur flows past Weinfelden. Arbon, Kreuzlingen and Romanshorn lie on Lake Constance.

52326.q: Which town in the canton of St Gallen lies on the Thur?
52326.e: The Thur flows past Wil before it reaches Thurgau. Rorschach lies on Lake Constance.

52327.q: Which three cantons does the Thur flow through?
52327.e: The Thur begins in St Gallen and flows through Thurgau. Finally, in the canton of Zurich, it flows into the Rhine.
52327.m: The Thur flows through St Gallen, Thurgau and Zurich.

52328.q: Roughly how long is the Thur?
52328.e: The Thur is about 135 kilometres long. It flows from the Toggenburg to the Rhine.
52328.m: The Thur is about 135 kilometres long.

52329.e: The Emme is a river in the canton of Bern. It flows through the Emmental.

52330.q: Which cheese with big holes is named after the valley of the Emme?
52330.e: Emmental cheese originally comes from the Emmental. It is known for its big holes.
52330.m: Emmental cheese comes from the valley of the Emme.

52331.q: Which river does the Emme flow into?
52331.e: The Emme flows into the Aare near Solothurn. The mouth lies between Zuchwil and Luterbach.
52331.m: The Emme flows into the Aare.

52332.q: In which canton does the Emme have its source?
52332.e: The Emme rises in the Bernese Prealps. After that it flows through the Emmental.
52332.m: The Emme rises in the canton of Bern.

52333.q: Which town in the canton of Bern with a big castle lies on the Emme?
52333.e: Burgdorf lies on the Emme at the entrance to the Emmental. Burgdorf Castle stands above the old town.

52334.q: What was the Emme especially feared for in the past?
52334.e: In a heavy thunderstorm the Emme can rise very quickly. Jeremias Gotthelf described the great flood of 1837 in “The Flood in the Emmental”.
52334.m: The Emme used to be feared for its floods.

52335.q: What is another river with a similar name in the canton of Lucerne called?
52335.e: The Kleine Emme (Little Emme) is a separate river in the canton of Lucerne. It flows into the Reuss at Emmenbrücke.
52335.m: The Kleine Emme is a different river from the Emme.

52336.q: Roughly how long is the Emme?
52336.e: The Emme is about 82 kilometres long. That makes it much shorter than the Aare.
52336.m: The Emme is about 80 kilometres long.

52337.q: In which direction does the Emme flow through the Emmental?
52337.e: The Emme comes from the Prealps in the south. It flows north to the Aare near Solothurn.
52337.m: The Emme flows north to the Aare.

52338.q: Why is Switzerland called the “water tower of Europe”?
a: Because many big rivers have their source here
Because it lies by the sea
Because there are many castles here
52338.e: Big rivers such as the Rhine, the Rhône and the Inn rise in the Swiss Alps. Their water flows into many countries in Europe.
52338.m: Switzerland is the water tower of Europe because big rivers rise here.

52339.q: In which mountains do the big Swiss rivers mostly have their source?
52339.e: The Rhine, the Rhône, the Inn and the Ticino all rise in the Alps. There is a lot of snow and there are many glaciers there.
52339.m: The big Swiss rivers rise in the Alps.

a: A line where water flows away in different directions
A dam that separates two lakes
A bridge that crosses a river
A filter that makes water clean
52340.e: On each side of a watershed rainwater flows into different rivers. There are many such lines in the Swiss Alps.
52340.m: At a watershed, water flows away in different directions.

52341.q: Which mountain massif is seen as the centre of the water tower, because several rivers flow from there in all directions?
52341.e: The Rhine, the Rhône, the Reuss and the Ticino all rise around the Gotthard. They flow north, south, east and west.
52341.m: Several big rivers rise around the Gotthard.

52342.q: What stores a lot of water as ice in the Alps?
52342.e: Glaciers are huge masses of ice. When they melt in summer, they release water into the rivers.

52343.q: Roughly how many lakes are there in Switzerland?
52343.e: There are about 1500 lakes in Switzerland. Many of them are small mountain lakes.

52344.q: What does Switzerland use the water of its rivers and reservoirs for especially often?
52344.e: With hydroelectric power stations Switzerland turns flowing water into electricity. More than half of the electricity produced in Switzerland comes from hydropower (as of 2024).
52344.m: Switzerland makes a lot of electricity from hydropower.

52345.q: At which pass in the Engadine does the water divide towards three different seas?
52345.e: Three big river basins meet at the Lunghin Pass. Depending on the side, a raindrop ends up in the North Sea, the Black Sea or the Adriatic.
52345.m: At the Lunghin Pass the ways to three seas divide.

52346.q: Where does most of the water from Switzerland flow to?
a: Into a big lake in the mountains
52346.e: Almost all of Switzerland's rivers flow across the border. That is how many countries in Europe get water from the Swiss Alps.
52346.m: Swiss water flows into the neighbouring countries.

52347.q: Which two cantons does the Gotthard Pass connect?
52347.e: The road over the Gotthard leads from Andermatt in the canton of Uri to Airolo in the canton of Ticino.
52347.m: The Gotthard Pass connects Uri with Ticino.

52348.q: Roughly how high is the Gotthard Pass?
52348.e: The top of the Gotthard Pass lies at about 2107 metres above sea level.
52348.m: The Gotthard Pass is just over 2100 metres high.

52349.q: What does the old Tremola road on the Gotthard have a lot of?
52349.e: The Tremola winds down with many bends from the top of the pass to Airolo. It is paved with stones.
52349.m: The Tremola is the winding cobbled road on the Gotthard.

52350.q: What is the famous bridge in the Schöllenen Gorge on the way to the Gotthard called?
52350.e: The Devil's Bridge crosses the Reuss in the Schöllenen Gorge near Andermatt. There is a well-known legend about it.
52350.m: The Devil's Bridge is in the Schöllenen Gorge.

52351.q: Which river flows through the Schöllenen Gorge on the Gotthard?
52351.e: The Reuss rises in the Gotthard area and flows down through the Schöllenen towards Lake Uri.
52351.m: The Reuss rushes through the Schöllenen Gorge.

52352.q: What has been a house for travellers at the top of the Gotthard Pass for centuries?
52352.e: There has been a hospice on the Gotthard since the Middle Ages. Travellers could spend the night and warm up there.
52352.m: Travellers found shelter in the hospice on the pass.

52353.q: Why is the Gotthard Pass road closed in winter?
a: Because of fog by the sea
Because of building work by the lake
52353.e: In winter there is a lot of snow on the pass and there is a danger of avalanches. That is why the road is closed for several months.
52353.m: In winter the Gotthard Pass is closed because of snow.

52354.q: In which year was the Gotthard road tunnel opened?
52354.e: The Gotthard road tunnel between Göschenen and Airolo was opened on 5 September 1980.
52354.m: Cars have driven through the Gotthard road tunnel since 1980.

52355.q: Which village lies at the northern foot of the Gotthard Pass in the canton of Uri?
52355.e: Andermatt lies in the Urseren Valley on the north side of the Gotthard. Airolo lies on the south side in Ticino.
52355.m: Andermatt lies on the Uri side of the Gotthard.

52356.q: What travels through the Gotthard Base Tunnel?
52356.e: The Gotthard Base Tunnel is a railway tunnel. That is why only trains travel through it.
52356.m: Only trains travel through the Gotthard Base Tunnel.

52357.q: Which record does the Gotthard Base Tunnel hold (as of 2025)?
a: Longest railway tunnel in the world
52357.e: At about 57 kilometres, the Gotthard Base Tunnel is the longest railway tunnel in the world (as of 2025).
52357.m: The Gotthard Base Tunnel is the longest railway tunnel in the world.

52358.q: Which canton do you reach when you travel from the north through the Gotthard Base Tunnel?
52358.e: The tunnel begins at Erstfeld in the canton of Uri and ends at Bodio in Ticino.
52358.m: The Base Tunnel takes you to Ticino.

52359.q: How many tubes does the Gotthard Base Tunnel have for the trains?
52359.e: The tunnel consists of two tubes. In each tube the trains travel in one direction only.
52359.m: The Gotthard Base Tunnel has two tubes.

52360.q: Why is the Gotthard Base Tunnel called a “base tunnel”?
a: It lies deep down at the foot of the mountain
It is the first tunnel in Switzerland
It leads to a military base
It has a station in the middle
52360.e: A base tunnel lies deep down, roughly at the level of the valleys. This means the trains hardly have to go uphill.
52360.m: A base tunnel runs flat through the foot of the mountain.

52361.q: What is an advantage of the Gotthard Base Tunnel for travellers?
a: The journey to Ticino is shorter
52361.e: Because the tunnel runs flat and straight through the mountain, trains reach Ticino faster than on the old mountain line.
52361.m: With the Base Tunnel you get to Ticino faster.

52362.q: Which country do you reach over the Great St Bernard from Valais?
52362.e: The Great St Bernard connects Valais with the Aosta Valley in Italy.
52362.m: Over the Great St Bernard you get to Italy.

52363.q: In which canton is the Swiss side of the Great St Bernard?
52363.e: The Great St Bernard lies in Lower Valais on the border with Italy.
52363.m: The Great St Bernard is in Valais.

52364.q: Roughly how high is the Great St Bernard?
52364.e: The top of the Great St Bernard Pass lies at about 2469 metres above sea level.
52364.m: The Great St Bernard is almost 2500 metres high.

52365.q: Who has looked after the hospice on the Great St Bernard for almost 1000 years?
52365.e: The hospice was founded in the 11th century. Canons live there, a kind of monk, who take in travellers.
52365.m: On the Great St Bernard, monks help travellers.

52366.q: Which famous dog is named after the Great St Bernard?
52366.e: The monks in the hospice on the Great St Bernard kept big dogs. They helped to find people in the snow. That is why they are called St Bernards.
52366.m: The St Bernard dog is named after the Great St Bernard.

52367.q: Which famous military leader crossed the Great St Bernard with his army in 1800?
52367.e: Napoleon Bonaparte crossed the Great St Bernard with many soldiers in May 1800 to march into Italy.
52367.m: Napoleon crossed the Great St Bernard in 1800.

52368.q: What lies right next to the hospice on the Great St Bernard?
52368.e: There is a small lake at the top of the pass. The border with Italy runs very close by.
52368.m: There is a small lake on the Great St Bernard.

52369.q: In winter, how do you get by car from Valais to Italy when the pass is closed?
52369.e: Since 1964 there has been a road tunnel under the Great St Bernard. It is open all year round.
52369.m: The tunnel under the Great St Bernard is open in winter too.

52370.q: Where does the St Bernard dog get its name from?
52370.e: These dogs were bred in the hospice on the Great St Bernard. That is why they are called St Bernards.
52370.m: The St Bernard dog is named after the Great St Bernard.

52371.q: What was the name of the most famous St Bernard rescue dog?
52371.e: Barry lived from 1800 to 1814 and worked for many years at the hospice on the Great St Bernard. He became famous as a lifesaver.
52371.m: Barry is the most famous St Bernard.

52372.q: How many people is the dog Barry said to have rescued?
52372.e: According to tradition, Barry rescued more than 40 people from the snow and cold. The exact number differs from source to source.

52373.q: Where can you see the stuffed dog Barry today?
a: In the Natural History Museum in Bern
In the Swiss National Museum in Zurich
In the Swiss Museum of Transport in Lucerne
52373.e: After his death Barry was preserved. Today he stands in the Natural History Museum in Bern.
52373.m: Barry stands in the Natural History Museum in Bern.

52374.q: What colours is a St Bernard's coat usually?
52374.e: St Bernards have a white coat with reddish-brown spots or patches.
52374.m: St Bernards are white with reddish-brown spots.

52375.q: How big are St Bernards compared with other dogs?
52375.e: St Bernards are among the biggest and heaviest dog breeds. They can weigh more than 60 kilograms.
52375.m: The St Bernard is a very big dog.

52376.q: What did St Bernards help the people in the hospice on the pass with in the past?
a: Finding people lost in the snow
52376.e: The dogs went with the helpers from the hospice and, with their good noses, found people who had got lost in the fog and snow.
52376.m: St Bernards searched for people lost in the snow.

52377.q: The St Bernard is seen as the national dog of which country?
52377.e: The St Bernard comes from Switzerland and is seen as the Swiss national dog.
52377.m: The St Bernard is the national dog of Switzerland.

52378.q: In which town in Valais can you visit St Bernards at the Barry Foundation today?
52378.e: The Fondation Barry in Martigny breeds St Bernards. You can visit the dogs at Barryland.
52378.m: You can visit St Bernards in Martigny.

52379.q: Which two countries does the Simplon Pass connect?
52379.e: The Simplon Pass leads from Brig in Valais to Domodossola in Italy.
52379.m: The Simplon Pass leads from Switzerland to Italy.

52380.q: At which town in Valais does the road over the Simplon Pass begin?
52380.e: The Simplon road starts in Brig in Upper Valais and then climbs up to the top of the pass.
52380.m: The Simplon road begins in Brig.

52381.q: Roughly how high is the Simplon Pass?
52381.e: At the top of the pass the Simplon road reaches about 2000 metres above sea level.
52381.m: The Simplon Pass is about 2000 metres high.

52382.q: Who had the first road for vehicles built over the Simplon around 1800?
52382.e: Napoleon wanted to get his cannons over the Alps. That is why he had the Simplon road built from 1801 to 1805.
52382.m: Napoleon had the Simplon road built.

52383.q: Which big stone animal stands on the Simplon Pass?
52383.e: A big stone eagle stands at the top of the pass. It is a reminder of the soldiers who guarded the border in the Second World War.
52383.m: A stone eagle stands on the Simplon Pass.

52384.q: What is the railway tunnel that runs under the Simplon Pass called?
52384.e: The Simplon Tunnel connects Brig with Iselle in Italy. It was opened in 1906.
52384.m: Under the Simplon, trains run through the Simplon Tunnel.

52385.q: Which rich merchant from Valais had a big palace built in Brig and used the Simplon for trade?
52385.e: In the 17th century Kaspar Jodok von Stockalper traded salt over the Simplon. His Stockalper Palace stands in Brig.
52385.m: Stockalper traded over the Simplon and built a palace in Brig.

52386.q: What is there for travellers on the Simplon Pass, similar to the Great St Bernard?
52386.e: A big hospice stands on the Simplon Pass. It is looked after by the same canons as the hospice on the Great St Bernard.
52386.m: There is a hospice on the Simplon Pass too.

52387.q: Which two cantons does the Furka Pass connect?
52387.e: The Furka Pass leads from Realp in the canton of Uri over to Goms in the canton of Valais.
52387.m: The Furka Pass connects Uri with Valais.

52388.q: Which big glacier lies right next to the Furka Pass?
52388.e: On the western side of the Furka there is a big glacier that reaches close to the pass road. Many people visit an ice grotto there.
52388.m: The Rhône Glacier lies near the Furka Pass.

52389.q: Which big lake does the Rhône, which rises at the Rhône Glacier, flow into?
52389.e: The Rhône rises at the Rhône Glacier near the Furka. It flows through Valais into Lake Geneva.
52389.m: The Rhône flows from the Rhône Glacier into Lake Geneva.

52390.q: Roughly how high is the Furka Pass?
52390.e: The top of the Furka Pass lies at about 2429 metres above sea level.
52390.m: The Furka Pass is about 2400 metres high.

52391.q: Which famous film agent drove over the Furka Pass in a film?
52391.e: In the 1964 James Bond film “Goldfinger” there is a car chase on the Furka road.
52391.m: James Bond drove over the Furka in the film “Goldfinger”.

52392.q: What can you visit at the Rhône Glacier on the Furka road?
a: An ice grotto in the glacier
52392.e: Every year an ice grotto is cut into the Rhône Glacier. You can walk through the blue ice inside it.
52392.m: There is an ice grotto in the Rhône Glacier.

52393.q: What kind of train runs over the old mountain line on the Furka in summer?
52393.e: The Furka Cogwheel Steam Railway runs in summer with old steam locomotives between Realp and Oberwald.
52393.m: A steam railway runs on the Furka in summer.

52394.q: How can cars be taken under the Furka in winter?
a: On a car train through the tunnel
52394.e: Car trains run through the Furka Base Tunnel between Realp and Oberwald. That way you can get to Valais in winter too.
52394.m: In winter cars go through the Furka Tunnel on the train.

52395.q: Which two cantons does the Grimsel Pass connect?
52395.e: The Grimsel Pass leads from Innertkirchen in the Bernese Oberland over to Upper Valais.
52395.m: The Grimsel Pass connects Bern with Valais.

52396.q: Roughly how high is the Grimsel Pass?
52396.e: The top of the Grimsel Pass lies at about 2164 metres above sea level.
52396.m: The Grimsel Pass is just over 2100 metres high.

52397.q: What do you see a lot of at the Grimsel?
52397.e: At the Grimsel several valleys were blocked with high walls. That is how big artificial lakes were created.
52397.m: There are many reservoirs at the Grimsel.

52398.q: What is the water of the reservoirs at the Grimsel used for?
52398.e: The water flows through pipes to power stations. There it drives turbines that produce electricity.

52399.q: What lies right next to the road at the top of the Grimsel Pass?
a: A farm with cows in the shed
52399.e: At the top of the Grimsel Pass the small Totensee lies right next to the road.
52399.m: There is a small lake on the Grimsel.

52400.q: What is the valley on the Bern side of the Grimsel Pass called?
52400.e: The Grimsel road climbs up through the Haslital. Meiringen and Innertkirchen lie there.
52400.m: The Haslital lies on the Bern side of the Grimsel.

52401.q: Which small place lies on the Valais side below the Grimsel and the Furka?
52401.e: Gletsch lies on the valley floor between the Grimsel Pass and the Furka Pass. From there you can drive over both passes.
52401.m: Gletsch lies between the Grimsel and the Furka.

52402.q: Which big reservoir lies near the top of the Grimsel Pass on the Bern side?
52402.e: Lake Grimsel is a reservoir behind a high dam. It lies near the top of the pass.
52402.m: Lake Grimsel is a reservoir at the Grimsel.

52403.q: Which two cantons does the Susten Pass connect?
52403.e: The Susten Pass leads from Innertkirchen in the canton of Bern into the Reuss valley of Uri.
52403.m: The Susten Pass connects Bern with Uri.

52404.q: Roughly how high is the Susten Pass?
52404.e: The top of the Susten Pass lies at about 2260 metres above sea level.
52404.m: The Susten Pass is just over 2200 metres high.

52405.q: Which glacier lies right next to the Susten road?
52405.e: Below the top of the pass on the Bern side lies the Stein Glacier. The Hotel Steingletscher stands next to it.
52405.m: The Stein Glacier lies on the Susten road.

52407.q: How does the Susten road get through the top of the pass?
52407.e: Right at the top the road goes through a short summit tunnel. After that it goes back down on the other side.
52407.m: At the top of the Susten you drive through a short tunnel.

52408.q: Which village in Uri lies at the end of the Susten road on the eastern side?
52408.e: On the Uri side the Susten road ends in Wassen in the Reuss valley. There it meets the Gotthard road.
52408.m: The Susten road ends in Wassen.

52409.q: Is the Susten Pass open to cars in winter?
52409.e: Because of snow and avalanches, the Susten Pass is closed for several months in winter.
52409.m: In winter the Susten Pass is closed.

52410.q: Which small lake lies by the Stein Glacier on the Susten?
52410.e: The Steinsee formed in front of the Stein Glacier when the ice melted.
52410.m: The Steinsee lies by the Stein Glacier.

52411.q: In which canton is the Julier Pass?
52411.e: The Julier Pass lies entirely in the canton of the Grisons in the east of Switzerland.
52411.m: The Julier Pass is in the Grisons.

52412.q: Which valley do you reach over the Julier Pass?
52412.e: The Julier road leads from the Oberhalbstein over the pass into a long high valley through which the Inn flows.
52412.m: Over the Julier Pass you drive into the Engadine.

52413.q: Roughly how high is the Julier Pass?
52413.e: The top of the Julier Pass lies at 2284 metres above sea level.
52413.m: The Julier Pass is almost 2300 metres high.

52414.q: Which old stone remains stand on the Julier Pass?
a: Boundary stones from the Middle Ages
52414.e: In Roman times there was a shrine on the Julier. The columns next to the road are remains of it.
52414.m: Columns from Roman times stand on the Julier.

52415.q: What do cars sometimes need in winter on snowy pass roads like the Julier?
52415.e: Snow chains are put around the wheels. This means cars slip less on snow and ice.
52415.m: Snow chains help cars on snowy roads.

52416.q: Which village at the Engadine end of the Julier Pass lies on a lake?
52416.e: Silvaplana lies on Lake Silvaplana in the Upper Engadine. This is where the Julier road ends.
52416.m: The Julier road ends in Silvaplana.

52417.q: Is the Julier Pass usually open in winter?
52417.e: The Julier Pass is cleared of snow in winter, so it can usually be driven on all year round.
52417.m: The Julier Pass is usually open in winter too.

52419.q: Which two cantons does the Lötschberg Tunnel connect?
52419.e: The old Lötschberg Tunnel leads from the Bernese Oberland under the mountain into Valais.
52419.m: The Lötschberg Tunnel connects Bern with Valais.

52420.q: At which village in the canton of Bern does the old Lötschberg Tunnel begin?
52420.e: The northern entrance of the old Lötschberg Tunnel is in Kandersteg. The southern entrance is in Goppenstein.
52420.m: The old Lötschberg Tunnel begins in Kandersteg.

52421.q: How can you travel by car through the old Lötschberg Tunnel?
a: On a road in the tunnel
52421.e: There is no road in the old Lötschberg Tunnel. Cars are carried on trains between Kandersteg and Goppenstein.
52421.m: Cars go through the Lötschberg on the train.

52422.q: In which year was the Lötschberg Base Tunnel opened?
52422.e: The Lötschberg Base Tunnel was opened in 2007. It lies much deeper than the old Lötschberg Tunnel.
52422.m: The Lötschberg Base Tunnel has been in use since 2007.

52423.q: Roughly how long is the Lötschberg Base Tunnel?
52423.e: The Lötschberg Base Tunnel is about 34.6 kilometres long. In the south you come out near Raron in Valais.
52423.m: The Lötschberg Base Tunnel is about 35 kilometres long.

52424.q: At which place does the Lötschberg Base Tunnel begin in the north?
52424.e: The northern entrance of the base tunnel is near Frutigen in the Kander valley. In the south you come out near Raron in Valais.
52424.m: The Lötschberg Base Tunnel begins near Frutigen.

52425.q: In which year was the old Lötschberg Tunnel opened?
52425.e: The old Lötschberg Tunnel is a railway tunnel and was opened in 1913.
52425.m: The old Lötschberg Tunnel has been open since 1913.

52426.q: Where do travellers from Bern get to faster thanks to the Lötschberg Tunnel?
52426.e: Trains run through the Lötschberg from Bern directly to Visp and Brig in Valais.
52426.m: Thanks to the Lötschberg you are soon in Valais.

52427.q: What sound does the horn of the PostBus make on mountain roads?
52427.e: The post horn plays three notes one after the other, which sound like “Tü-ta-to”.

52428.q: Why does the PostBus sound its horn before tight bends on pass roads?
a: So that others hear it coming
52428.e: On tight bends you cannot see the oncoming traffic. The horn warns others that a big bus is coming.
