52428.m: The PostBus sounds its horn as a warning before tight bends.

52429.q: Who has right of way on roads with the blue “mountain postal road” sign?
52429.e: On a mountain postal road the other vehicles must make way for the PostBus and follow the driver's instructions.
52429.m: On mountain postal roads the PostBus has right of way.

52430.q: What is shown on the sign for a mountain postal road?
52430.e: The sign is blue and shows a yellow post horn. It shows that the PostBus has right of way here.
52430.m: A yellow post horn marks a mountain postal road.

52431.q: When do PostBuses drive over most of the high Alpine passes?
52431.e: Most passes are closed in winter because of snow. That is why the pass PostBuses run mainly in summer.
52431.m: The PostBus goes over the high passes in summer.

52432.q: Apart from travellers, what did the PostBus carry in the past?
52432.e: The PostBus replaced the mail coach. It brought people, but also letters and parcels, to the villages.
52432.m: In the past the PostBus also brought letters and parcels.

52433.q: What travelled over the passes before there were PostBuses?
52433.e: In the past horses pulled the mail coaches over the passes. Later the PostBuses replaced the coaches.
52433.m: Before the PostBus, the mail coach went over the passes.

52434.q: Why is a very tight bend called a “hairpin bend”?
a: It is as thin as a hair
It was built by a hairdresser
52434.e: The road turns almost completely back on itself. From above this looks like a bent hairpin.
52434.m: A hairpin bend has the shape of a hairpin.

52435.q: Why do pass roads have lots of hairpin bends?
a: So that the road is not too steep
So that the road is shorter
So that you can drive faster
So that you see more trees
52435.e: The road zigzags up the mountain. That makes it less steep than if it went straight up.
52435.m: Hairpin bends make a mountain road less steep.

52436.q: What is another name for a hairpin bend?
52436.e: Hairpin bends are also called switchbacks, because the road almost turns back.
52436.m: A hairpin bend is also called a switchback.

52437.q: How should a car drive through a hairpin bend?
52437.e: In a hairpin bend you cannot see far and the bend is tight. That is why you must drive slowly.
52437.m: You drive slowly in hairpin bends.

52438.q: Seen from above, what shape does a pass road with many hairpin bends have?
52438.e: The road goes back and forth up the mountain. From above it looks like a zigzag or a snake.
52438.m: Seen from above, many bends look like a zigzag.

52439.q: What often stands at the edge of hairpin bends so that cars do not leave the road?
52439.e: Crash barriers or walls at the roadside stop vehicles if they go too wide on the bend.
52439.m: Crash barriers protect cars on tight bends.

52440.q: Who often has to swing out wide to get round a tight hairpin bend?
52440.e: Long vehicles such as PostBuses or coaches need a lot of space on tight bends. That is why they need the whole width of the road.
52440.m: Long buses need a lot of space on hairpin bends.

52441.q: Which cycle race sometimes goes over Swiss passes with hairpin bends?
52441.e: The Tour de Suisse is a cycle race through Switzerland. The professionals often ride over steep passes.
52441.m: The Tour de Suisse often goes over passes.

52442.q: In which year was the first railway tunnel through the Gotthard opened?
52442.e: The old Gotthard railway tunnel between Göschenen and Airolo was opened in 1882. At that time it was the longest tunnel in the world.
52442.m: Trains have run through the Gotthard since 1882.

52443.q: Which river rises in the Grimsel area and flows through the Haslital?
52443.e: The Aare rises at the Aare glaciers near the Grimsel. It flows through the Haslital into Lake Brienz.
52443.m: The Aare comes from the Grimsel.

52444.q: Between which two mountain ranges does the Swiss Plateau lie?
a: The Black Forest and the Alps
52444.e: The Swiss Plateau lies between the Jura in the north-west and the Alps in the south.
52444.m: The Swiss Plateau lies between the Jura and the Alps.

52445.q: Which motorway runs right across the Swiss Plateau from Geneva to St Gallen?
52445.e: The A1 connects many big cities on the Swiss Plateau, for example Lausanne, Bern and Zurich.
52445.m: The A1 runs right across the Swiss Plateau.

52446.q: What does the landscape on the Swiss Plateau usually look like?
52446.e: On the Swiss Plateau there are gentle hills, fields, forests, lakes and many towns.
52446.m: The Swiss Plateau is hilly and has many fields.

52447.q: Which big city lies on the Swiss Plateau?
52447.e: Zurich is the biggest city in Switzerland and lies on the Swiss Plateau. The other places are in the mountains.
52447.m: Zurich lies on the Swiss Plateau.

52448.q: Which river flows right across the Swiss Plateau and through Bern?
52448.e: The Aare flows through Bern, Solothurn and Aarau. It is the longest river that flows entirely within Switzerland.
52448.m: The Aare flows through Bern and the Swiss Plateau.

52449.q: Why are there so many farms on the Swiss Plateau?
52449.e: On the Swiss Plateau the soil is fertile and the land is not so steep. That is why grain, potatoes and vegetables grow well there.
52449.m: The soil on the Swiss Plateau is fertile.

52450.q: Which big lake lies in the far south-west of Switzerland?
52450.e: Lake Geneva lies in the far south-west of Switzerland. It is the biggest lake that Switzerland has a share of.
52450.m: Lake Geneva lies in the south-west of Switzerland.

52451.q: Roughly how much of Switzerland's area is Swiss Plateau?
52451.e: The Swiss Plateau makes up about 30 per cent of Switzerland's area. That is roughly a third.
52451.m: The Swiss Plateau is about a third of Switzerland.

52452.q: In which part of Switzerland are the Jura Mountains?
52452.e: The Jura stretches across the north-west of Switzerland from Geneva to the area around Schaffhausen.
52452.m: The Jura lies in the north-west of Switzerland.

52453.q: Which rock is the Jura mainly made of?
52453.e: The Jura is mainly made of limestone. You often find fossilised shells and caves in it.
52453.m: The Jura is mainly made of limestone.

52454.q: Are the mountains in the Jura higher or lower than the Alps?
52454.e: The highest Jura peaks in Switzerland are only about 1700 metres high. In the Alps there are peaks over 4000 metres.
52454.m: The Jura mountains are lower than the Alps.

52455.q: Which craft has long been famous in the Jura?
52455.e: In the Jura, for example in La Chaux-de-Fonds, watches have been made for centuries.
52455.m: The Jura is famous for its watchmakers.

52456.q: Which Jura mountain above Lake Biel has a tall transmitter tower?
52456.e: The Chasseral is 1606 metres high. Next to the summit stands a transmitter tower 120 metres tall.
52456.m: There is a transmitter tower on the Chasseral.

52457.q: What is the huge rock basin in the Neuchâtel Jura called?
52457.e: The Creux du Van is a big rock basin with high, curved cliffs in the canton of Neuchâtel.
52457.m: The Creux du Van is a rock basin in the Jura.

52458.q: Which period of the dinosaurs is named after the Jura?
52458.e: The rocks in the Jura gave a period of Earth's history its name. Many dinosaurs lived in the Jurassic.
52458.m: The Jurassic is named after the Jura Mountains.

52459.q: Which big bird of prey also hunts marmots in the Alps?
52459.e: The golden eagle has very sharp eyes and strong talons. It is big and strong enough to hunt hares and marmots.
52459.m: The golden eagle hunts in the Alps.

52460.q: Which white flower with felty leaves grows high up in the Alps?
52460.e: Edelweiss grows on stony meadows in the mountains. It is protected and must not be picked.
52460.m: Edelweiss grows high up in the Alps.

52461.q: Which nimble animal with short, hook-shaped horns leaps over rocks?
52461.e: The chamois is very agile and leaps safely over steep rocks. Its horns are bent like a hook at the end.
52461.m: The chamois leaps safely over rocks.

52462.q: Which animal with long, curved horns climbs in the Alps?
52462.e: The ibex lives high up among the rocks. The males have long, curved horns.
52462.m: The ibex climbs among the rocks of the Alps.

52463.q: What is the way over a mountain from one valley to another called?
52463.e: A pass is the lowest point between two mountains. Roads lead over it from one valley to the next.
52463.m: A pass takes you from one valley to another.

a: Snow that slides down the slope
A storm on a mountain lake
A big rock in the river
52464.e: In an avalanche a lot of snow breaks loose and slides quickly down the mountain. Avalanches can be very dangerous.
52464.m: An avalanche is snow sliding down a mountain.

52465.q: Which two big rivers rise in the Swiss Alps?
52465.e: The Rhine and the Rhône have their sources in the Swiss Alps in the Gotthard area.
52465.m: The Rhine and the Rhône rise in the Alps.

52466.q: How does the temperature change when you climb a high mountain?
a: It gets colder first and then warmer
52466.e: For every 100 metres of height it gets on average just over half a degree colder. That is why there is often snow at the top.
52466.m: The higher you climb, the colder it gets.

a: Between the Swiss Plateau and the Alps
In the middle of the Jura
52467.e: The Prealps form the transition from the flat Swiss Plateau to the high Alps.
52467.m: The Prealps lie between the Swiss Plateau and the Alps.

52468.q: What is there usually none of in the Prealps?
52468.e: The Prealps are lower than the High Alps. That is why there are hardly any glaciers there, but many meadows and forests.
52468.m: There are hardly any glaciers in the Prealps.

52469.q: Which mountain near Lucerne is called the “Queen of the Mountains”?
52469.e: The Rigi lies between Lake Lucerne and Lake Zug. From the top there is a beautiful view.
52469.m: The Rigi is called the “Queen of the Mountains”.

52470.q: What do farmers do in summer with the grass on steep slopes in the Prealps?
a: They mow it and make hay
52470.e: The grass is mown and dried. The cows eat the hay in winter.
52470.m: Farmers make hay from the grass for the winter.

52471.q: What do farmers do with their cows in summer in the Prealps?
a: They drive them up to the alpine pasture
They keep them in the shed
They bring them down into the valley
They take them to the city
52471.e: In summer the farmers take the cows up to the alpine pasture. There they eat fresh grass.
52471.m: In summer the cows go up to the alpine pasture.

52472.q: Which railway was the first mountain railway in Europe, running up a mountain from 1871?
52472.e: The Vitznau-Rigi railway was opened in 1871. It was the first mountain railway in Europe.
52472.m: The Rigi Railway is the oldest mountain railway in Europe.

52473.q: Which Prealpine mountain rises in the Gruyère region in the canton of Fribourg?
52473.e: The Moléson is a well-known viewpoint mountain in the Gruyère region. Gruyère cheese is made in this area.
52473.m: The Moléson is the local mountain of the Gruyère region.

52474.q: In which canton is the Engadine?
52474.e: The Engadine is a long high valley in the canton of the Grisons in the east of Switzerland.
52474.m: The Engadine is in the Grisons.

52475.q: Which river flows through the Engadine?
52475.e: In Romansh the Inn is called “En”. That is where the Engadine gets its name.
52475.m: The Inn flows through the Engadine.

52476.q: Which language do many people in the Engadine speak besides German?
52476.e: Romansh is one of the four national languages of Switzerland. It is still often spoken in the Engadine.
52476.m: Romansh is spoken in the Engadine.

52477.q: Which well-known holiday resort in the Engadine has hosted the Olympics twice?
52477.e: The Winter Olympics took place in St Moritz in 1928 and 1948.
52477.m: St Moritz has hosted the Olympics twice.

52478.q: What is the children's book about a boy from the Engadine and a bell called?
52478.e: Ursli wants to carry the biggest bell at the spring festival. The story takes place in Guarda.
52478.m: Ursli with his bell comes from the Engadine.

52479.q: Which festival do children in the Engadine celebrate with bells on 1 March?
52479.e: At Chalandamarz the children go through the village with bells and drive away the winter.
52479.m: At Chalandamarz the children ring the winter away.

52480.q: Which pastry with nuts is a speciality from the Engadine?
52480.e: The Engadine nut tart is filled with walnuts and caramel.
52480.m: The Engadine nut tart is filled with nuts.

52481.q: Which famous cross-country skiing race takes place in the Engadine every year?
52481.e: In the Engadine Ski Marathon thousands of people ski cross-country from Maloja to S-chanf.
52481.m: The Engadine Ski Marathon is a cross-country ski race.

52482.q: Where does the water of the Inn end up?
52482.e: The Inn flows into Austria and joins the Danube at Passau. The Danube flows into the Black Sea.
52482.m: The water of the Inn reaches the Black Sea.

52483.q: Which caves on Lake Thun are named after a monk who is said to have driven away a dragon?
52483.e: According to legend, the monk Beatus drove a dragon out of the cave. Today you can visit the stalactite cave.
52483.m: The St Beatus Caves lie on Lake Thun.

52484.q: Which viewpoint right above Interlaken can be reached by funicular?
52484.e: The Harder funicular runs from Interlaken up to Harder Kulm. From there you can see two lakes and many mountains.

52485.q: What is the open-air museum with old Swiss houses near Brienz called?
52485.e: At Ballenberg there are over a hundred old houses from all over Switzerland. You can see how people used to live.
52485.m: There are old Swiss houses at Ballenberg.

52486.q: What is the Lauterbrunnen valley especially known for?
52486.e: In the Lauterbrunnen valley many waterfalls plunge over steep cliffs, for example the Staubbach Falls.
52486.m: There are many waterfalls in the Lauterbrunnen valley.

52487.q: What can you see on the Schynige Platte near Interlaken?
52487.e: Hundreds of mountain plants grow in the alpine garden on the Schynige Platte. You go up on an old cog railway.
52487.m: There is an alpine garden on the Schynige Platte.

52488.q: Which canton does the Bernese Oberland belong to?
52488.e: The Bernese Oberland is the southern, mountainous part of the canton of Bern.
52488.m: The Bernese Oberland belongs to the canton of Bern.

52489.q: Which famous ski race takes place in Wengen every year?
52489.e: The best skiers in the world race on the Lauberhorn near Wengen. The downhill is said to be the longest in the World Cup.
52489.m: The Lauberhorn race takes place in Wengen.

52490.q: On which mountain above Mürren is there a revolving restaurant?
52490.e: The restaurant on the Schilthorn slowly turns in a circle. That way you can see all the mountains around while you eat.
52490.m: There is a revolving restaurant on the Schilthorn.

52491.q: Which pass connects Meiringen with the canton of Obwalden?
52491.e: Cars and trains travel over the Brünig Pass from the Bernese Oberland to Obwalden.
52491.m: The Brünig Pass leads from Meiringen to Obwalden.

52492.q: What do the cheesemakers in the Emmental make in big copper vats?
52492.e: The milk is heated in the copper vat and thickened. Big wheels of cheese are made from it.
52492.m: In the copper vat milk becomes cheese.

52493.q: What is the small house next to an Emmental farm, where the grandparents often live, called?
52493.e: When the young people take over the farm, the parents move into the Stöckli next to the big house.
52493.m: The grandparents often live in the Stöckli.

52494.q: What does the landscape in the Emmental look like?
52494.e: The Emmental is a hilly landscape with meadows, forests and scattered farms.
52494.m: There are lots of green hills in the Emmental.

52495.q: Which sport in sawdust is very popular in the Emmental?
52495.e: In Swiss wrestling (Schwingen) two men or women in special canvas shorts wrestle in sawdust. There are many well-known wrestlers in the Emmental.
52495.m: Swiss wrestling is very popular in the Emmental.

52496.q: What is typical of the old farmhouses in the Emmental?
52496.e: Emmental farmhouses have huge roofs that reach almost to the ground.

52497.q: What kind of bridges do you often see in the Emmental?
52497.e: Several old wooden bridges with a roof cross the Emme. This keeps the wood dry.
52497.m: There are covered wooden bridges in the Emmental.

52498.q: Which viewpoint mountain, about 1400 metres high, lies on the edge of the Emmental?
52498.e: The Napf is about 1400 metres high and lies on the border between the cantons of Bern and Lucerne. From the top you can see far across the hills.
52498.m: The Napf is a viewpoint mountain by the Emmental.

52499.q: What can you find in the streams around the Napf if you are lucky?
52499.e: There are tiny flakes of gold in the Napf streams. You can wash them out with a pan.
52499.m: There is gold in the Napf streams.

52500.q: Which glacier is the biggest in the Alps?
52500.e: The Great Aletsch Glacier is the biggest glacier in the whole of the Alps. It has more ice than any other Alpine glacier.
52500.m: The Aletsch Glacier is the biggest glacier in the Alps.

52501.q: In which canton is the Aletsch Glacier?
52501.e: The Aletsch Glacier flows down the south side of the Bernese Alps into Valais.
52501.m: The Aletsch Glacier is in Valais.

52502.q: Roughly how long is the Aletsch Glacier?
52502.e: The Aletsch Glacier is about 20 kilometres long. But because of the warmth it gets shorter every year.
52502.m: The Aletsch Glacier is about 20 kilometres long.

52503.q: What is happening to the Aletsch Glacier because it is getting warmer and warmer?
52503.e: Because it is getting warmer, more ice melts than new ice is added. That is why the Aletsch Glacier gets shorter every year.
52503.m: The Aletsch Glacier is getting shorter because of the warmth.

52504.q: Which UNESCO World Heritage Site does the Aletsch Glacier belong to?
52504.e: The Jungfrau-Aletsch area was listed in 2001 as the first natural World Heritage Site in the Alps.
52504.m: The Aletsch Glacier belongs to the Jungfrau-Aletsch World Heritage Site.

52505.q: From which viewpoint mountain do you get a good view of the Aletsch Glacier?
52505.e: From the Eggishorn near Fiesch you can see far across the long river of ice.
52505.m: You can see the Aletsch Glacier from the Eggishorn.

52506.q: Does the ice of the Aletsch Glacier move?
a: Yes, it slowly flows down the valley
52506.e: Glacier ice is heavy and flows very slowly down the valley, at the Aletsch up to about 200 metres a year.
52506.m: Glacier ice slowly flows down the valley.

52507.q: Which very old trees grow in the Aletsch Forest above the glacier?
52507.e: In the Aletsch Forest there are Swiss stone pines that are several hundred years old. Swiss stone pines grow high up in the mountains.
52507.m: Ancient Swiss stone pines grow in the Aletsch Forest.

52508.q: Why are the glaciers in Switzerland melting?
a: It is getting warmer and warmer
52508.e: Because of climate change it is getting warmer. In summer more ice melts than new ice is added in winter.
52508.m: The glaciers are melting because it is getting warmer.

52509.q: Roughly how many glaciers are there in Switzerland?
52509.e: There are about 1400 glaciers in Switzerland. Many of them are very small.

52510.q: What is part of the ice at the Rhône Glacier covered with in summer?
52510.e: White sheets reflect the sunlight. This makes the ice near the ice grotto melt a little more slowly.
52510.m: White sheets protect the ice from the sun.

52511.q: What is often left behind when a glacier melts?
52511.e: The glacier leaves rubble behind. In hollows the meltwater collects to form new lakes.
52511.m: Where a glacier melts, stones and lakes are left behind.

52512.q: What is the meltwater from glaciers important for in summer?
52512.e: In hot summers meltwater fills the rivers. Without glaciers some streams then carry less water.
52512.m: Glaciers give water to the rivers in summer.

52513.q: Which glacier was given a farewell with a funeral ceremony in 2019?
52513.e: The Pizol Glacier in the canton of St Gallen had almost completely disappeared. So people held a funeral ceremony for it.
52513.m: The Pizol Glacier was given a farewell in 2019.

52514.q: On a glacier trail, how can you see where the ice used to be?
a: From signs with years on them
From colourful flags on the ice
52514.e: On the way to some glaciers, for example the Morteratsch Glacier, signs show where the ice used to be. The glacier has already retreated a long way.
52514.m: Signs show where the glacier used to be.

52515.q: In which year did the Swiss glaciers lose a particularly large amount of ice, about 6 per cent?
52515.e: The summer of 2022 was very hot and dry. The Swiss glaciers lost about 6 per cent of their ice.
52515.m: A particularly large amount of glacier ice melted in 2022.

52516.q: How many national parks are there in Switzerland?
52516.e: The Swiss National Park is the only national park in Switzerland.

52517.q: In which canton is the Swiss National Park?
52517.e: The national park lies in the east of Switzerland, in the Lower Engadine in the canton of the Grisons.
52517.m: The national park is in the Grisons.

52518.q: In which year was the Swiss National Park founded?
52518.e: The park was founded in 1914. It is the oldest national park in the Alps.
52518.m: The national park was founded in 1914.

52519.q: What are you not allowed to do in the national park?
52519.e: In the national park nature should remain undisturbed. That is why you must not pick anything and must stay on the paths.
52519.m: You do not pick flowers in the national park.

52520.q: Which big bird was released back into the wild in the national park?
52520.e: The bearded vulture had died out in the Alps. From 1991 young bearded vultures were released in the national park.
52520.m: Bearded vultures were released in the national park.

52521.q: Which big animal with antlers do you often see in the national park?
52521.e: In autumn you can hear the red deer stags roaring in the national park.
52521.m: Many red deer live in the national park.

52522.q: Are you allowed to take your dog into the national park?
52522.e: Dogs could disturb the wild animals. That is why they are not allowed in the national park, not even on a lead.
52522.m: Dogs are not allowed in the national park.

52523.q: In which village is the national park's visitor centre?
52523.e: The visitor centre in Zernez has an exhibition about the park's animals and plants.
52523.m: The national park's visitor centre is in Zernez.

52524.q: Which string instrument belongs to the folk music of the Toggenburg?
52524.e: The Toggenburg Halszither is a cittern with a long neck and metal strings. It is a typical instrument of folk music in the Toggenburg.
52524.m: The Halszither belongs to Toggenburg music.

52525.q: Which peak of the Churfirsten can you reach by cable car from the Toggenburg?
52525.e: From Unterwasser you first go to Iltios and then take the cable car up the Chäserrugg. At the top there is a wooden restaurant.
52525.m: A cable car goes up the Chäserrugg.

52526.q: How many peaks are usually counted in the Churfirsten?
52526.e: The Churfirsten are usually counted as seven peaks, though more or fewer depending on how you count. On the south side they drop steeply down to Lake Walen.
52526.m: The Churfirsten are usually counted as seven peaks.

52527.q: Which famous reformer was born in the Toggenburg in 1484?
52527.e: Ulrich Zwingli was born in the upper Toggenburg. Later he worked as a priest in Zurich.
52527.m: Ulrich Zwingli came from the Toggenburg.

52528.q: What can you do on the Sound Trail in the Toggenburg?
52528.e: Along the Sound Trail there are instruments made of wood and metal. You can play them and experience sounds.
52528.m: On the Sound Trail you can try out sounds.

52529.q: Which animal is named after the Toggenburg?
52529.e: The Toggenburg goat is a brown breed of goat with white stripes on its head.
52529.m: The Toggenburg goat is named after the valley.

52530.q: Which art is an old tradition in the Toggenburg?
52530.e: Toggenburg farmhouse painting shows cows going up to the alpine pastures, cows and farmers in bright colours.
52530.m: In the Toggenburg people paint colourful farm pictures.

52531.q: Which two villages in the upper Toggenburg are well-known holiday resorts?
52531.e: Wildhaus and Unterwasser lie in the upper Toggenburg. In winter people ski there, in summer they go hiking.
52531.m: Wildhaus and Unterwasser lie in the Toggenburg.

52532.q: Which dark bread is a speciality from Valais?
52532.e: Valais rye bread is baked from rye flour. Rye also grows in the high mountain valleys.

52533.q: What is the capital of the canton of Valais called?
52533.e: Sion is called Sitten in German. The cantonal government sits there.
52533.m: Sion is the capital of Valais.

52534.q: Why do the old wooden storehouses in Valais stand on round stone slabs?
a: So that no mice can climb in
So that they do not fall over
So that they stay warm in winter
So that they can be moved
52534.e: The old storehouses are called Stadel. Mice cannot climb over the round stone slabs, so they cannot get to the grain.
52534.m: The stone slabs under the storehouses keep mice out.

52535.q: What is special about the mountain village of Zermatt?
a: It lies on a big lake
There is never any snow there
52535.e: No normal cars drive in Zermatt. You arrive by train and get around the village in small electric vehicles.

52536.q: What is the weather often like in the Rhône valley in Valais?
52536.e: High mountains keep out many rain clouds. That is why it is often sunny and dry in the Rhône valley.
52536.m: It is often sunny and dry in Valais.

52537.q: Which cheese dish comes from Valais?
52537.e: For raclette half a wheel of cheese is melted. You eat the soft cheese with potatoes.
52537.m: Raclette is a cheese dish from Valais.

52538.q: Which orange fruit grows in especially large amounts in Valais?
52538.e: Many apricots grow in Valais. They are used to make jam, for example.

52539.q: Which train travels slowly from Zermatt to St Moritz?
52539.e: The Glacier Express takes about eight hours to travel through the Alps from Zermatt to St Moritz.
52539.m: The Glacier Express runs from Zermatt to St Moritz.

52540.q: How many stars are there on the flag of Valais?
52540.e: The 13 stars stand for the 13 old “Zenden”, or districts, of Valais.

52541.q: In which language is Switzerland called “Svizra”?
52541.e: In Romansh Switzerland is called “Svizra”. In Italian it is called “Svizzera”, in French “Suisse”.
52541.m: In Romansh Switzerland is called Svizra.

52542.q: How do you say “Good day” in Italian?
52542.e: “Buongiorno” means “Good day” in Italian. You often hear this greeting in Ticino.

52543.q: What is the biggest bilingual town in Switzerland called?
52543.e: In Biel/Bienne many people speak German and many speak French. The street signs are written in both languages.
52543.m: Biel/Bienne is the biggest bilingual town in Switzerland.

52544.q: What do people in German-speaking Switzerland mostly speak in everyday life?
52544.e: In everyday life most people in German-speaking Switzerland speak dialect, that is Swiss German. At school they also learn Standard German.
52544.m: In German-speaking Switzerland people mostly speak dialect in everyday life.

52545.q: What colours is the Swiss flag?
52545.e: The Swiss flag is red with a white cross in the middle.
52545.m: The Swiss flag is red and white.

52546.q: What can you see on the Swiss flag?
52546.e: In the middle of the red flag there is a white cross. It is a symbol of Switzerland.
52546.m: There is a white cross on the Swiss flag.

52548.q: Which symbol looks like the Swiss flag with the colours swapped?
52548.e: The symbol of the Red Cross is a red cross on a white background. It honours Switzerland by reversing its colours.
52548.m: The Red Cross symbol has the colours of the Swiss flag swapped.

52549.q: What lights up in many places in Switzerland on 1 August?
52549.e: On the national holiday bonfires burn on many hills. Children carry paper lanterns with the Swiss cross.
52549.m: Paper lanterns and bonfires light up on 1 August.

52550.q: What do many Swiss products show so that you can see they come from Switzerland?
52550.e: Many products from Switzerland carry a small Swiss cross. There are clear rules about when it may be used.
52550.m: The Swiss cross shows that something comes from Switzerland.

52551.q: Which canton is the biggest in Switzerland?
52551.e: The Grisons have the largest area of all the cantons. There are many mountains and valleys there.
52551.m: The Grisons are the biggest canton.

52552.q: In which canton do the most people live?
52552.e: The canton of Zurich has the most inhabitants. There are over 1.5 million people (as of 2024).
52552.m: The most people live in the canton of Zurich.

52554.q: Which three cantons are seen as the founders of Switzerland?
52554.e: Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden formed an alliance in 1291. This is seen as the beginning of Switzerland.
52554.m: Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden are the founding cantons.

52555.q: What is written before the number on Swiss number plates?
52555.e: Every Swiss number plate shows the canton's abbreviation, for example ZH for Zurich or BE for Bern.
52555.m: The canton's abbreviation is on every number plate.

52556.q: Which animal can you see on the coat of arms of Bern?
52556.e: A black bear walks across the coat of arms of Bern. The bear is the symbol of the city.
52556.m: The bear is the heraldic animal of Bern.

52557.q: Which animals can you visit in a park on the bank of the Aare in Bern?
52557.e: Bears live in the Bear Park in Bern. They used to live in the bear pit right next to it.
52557.m: Bears live in the Bear Park in Bern.

52558.q: What is the famous clock tower in Bern's old town called?
52558.e: The Zytglogge is an old tower with an astronomical clock. Shortly before every full hour, figures move on it.
52558.m: The Zytglogge is the famous clock tower of Bern.

52559.q: What are the covered walkways in Bern's old town called?
52559.e: There are many arcades in Bern's old town. Under them you can shop and stay dry even when it rains.
52559.m: In Bern's old town you walk under arcades.

52560.q: Which vegetable is the star of Bern's Zibelemärit in November?
52560.e: “Zibele” means onion. At the Zibelemärit (onion market) stallholders sell lots of onions, often plaited into strings.
52560.m: At Bern's Zibelemärit everything is about onions.

52561.q: How many members does the Federal Council, which governs in Bern, have?
52561.e: The Federal Council is the government of Switzerland. It has seven members.
52561.m: The Federal Council has seven members.

52562.q: Which neighbouring country lies to the east of Switzerland?
52562.e: To the east Switzerland borders Austria and the small country of Liechtenstein.
52562.m: Austria lies to the east of Switzerland.

52563.q: Which is Switzerland's smallest neighbouring country?
52563.e: Liechtenstein is a very small country between Switzerland and Austria. It is smaller than many cantons.

52564.q: On which big lake do Switzerland, Germany and Austria meet?
52564.e: Lake Constance lies in the north-east of Switzerland. Its shores belong to Switzerland, Germany and Austria.
52564.m: Three countries meet at Lake Constance.

52565.q: What does Switzerland not have, because it lies in the middle of Europe?
52565.e: Switzerland is a landlocked country. It has no coast, but many lakes and rivers.
52565.m: Switzerland is not by the sea.

52566.e: Switzerland lies in the middle of Europe. That is why many trains and lorries travel through Switzerland.
52566.m: Switzerland lies in the middle of Europe.

52567.q: What does Switzerland look like on the map?
52567.e: From west to east Switzerland is about 350 kilometres wide. From north to south it is only about 220 kilometres.
52567.m: Switzerland is wider than it is tall.

52568.q: Which canton forms the tip in the far south on the map?
52568.e: On the map Ticino sticks out to the south like a point. It lies south of the Alps.
52568.m: Ticino is the southern tip of Switzerland.

52569.q: Which canton lies in the far west on the map?
52569.e: Geneva lies in the far west of Switzerland. The canton is almost completely surrounded by France.
52569.m: Geneva lies in the far west of Switzerland.

52570.q: Which canton lies in the far east on the map?
52570.e: The Grisons form the easternmost part of Switzerland. There Switzerland borders Austria and Italy.
52570.m: The Grisons lie in the far east of Switzerland.

52571.q: Which big waterfall lies in the north of Switzerland near Schaffhausen?
52571.e: The Rhine Falls are one of the biggest waterfalls in Europe. They lie at Neuhausen am Rheinfall in the canton of Schaffhausen.
52571.m: The Rhine Falls are near Schaffhausen.

52572.q: Where do three countries meet in Basel?
52572.e: In Basel, Switzerland, Germany and France meet on the Rhine. This point is called the Three Countries Corner.
52572.m: Three countries meet at the Three Countries Corner in Basel.

52573.q: Which milk is Gruyère cheese made from?
52573.e: Gruyère is made from raw cow's milk. The milk comes from cows in the region.
52573.m: Gruyère is made from cow's milk.

52574.q: What does a Gruyère cheese usually look like inside?
52574.e: Gruyère has almost no holes. Its paste is firm and even.

52575.q: In German this cheese is called Greyerzer. What is it called in French?
52575.e: In French the cheese is called “Le Gruyère”. It is named after the Gruyère region (Greyerz in German).
52575.m: Greyerzer is called Gruyère in French.

52576.q: What kind of cheese is Gruyère?
52576.e: Gruyère is a hard cheese. It matures for many months and becomes firm as it does.

52577.q: What is the minimum time a Gruyère matures for?
52577.e: A Gruyère must mature in the cellar for at least about five months. Many wheels mature even longer and then taste stronger.
52577.m: A Gruyère matures for many months.

52578.q: Roughly how heavy is a whole wheel of Gruyère?
52578.e: A wheel of Gruyère usually weighs between 25 and 40 kilograms. It is round and flat.
52578.m: A wheel of Gruyère is very heavy.

52579.q: Which hot dish is Gruyère often needed for?
52579.e: Gruyère melts well. That is why it is in many recipes for cheese fondue.

52580.q: Where are the wheels of Gruyère looked after while they mature?
52580.e: The wheels lie in a damp, cool cellar. There they are regularly turned and rubbed with salt water.
52580.m: Gruyère matures in a cool cellar.

52581.q: What is the person who makes cheese from milk called?
52581.e: A cheesemaker makes cheese from milk in the cheese dairy.
52581.m: The cheesemaker turns milk into cheese.

52582.q: How can you recognise an Emmental cheese straight away?
52582.e: Emmental has big, round holes. That is why it is known all over the world.

52583.q: In which canton is the Emmental?
52583.e: The Emmental is a hilly area in the canton of Bern. The cheese gets its name from there.
52583.m: The Emmental is in the canton of Bern.

52584.q: What is the firm outer layer of a wheel of Emmental called?
52584.e: The rind is the hard outer layer of the cheese wheel. It protects the cheese inside while it matures.
52584.m: The rind protects the Emmental while it matures.

52585.q: What forms inside Emmental so that holes grow?
52585.e: Tiny bacteria in the cheese produce a gas as it matures. The gas collects and that is how the holes form.
52585.m: Gas makes the holes in Emmental.

52586.q: How heavy can a big wheel of Emmental get?
52586.e: A wheel of Emmental weighs about 75 to 120 kilograms. It is one of the biggest cheese wheels in the world.
52586.m: A wheel of Emmental is enormously heavy.

52587.q: What does Emmental usually taste like?
52587.e: Young Emmental tastes mild and slightly nutty. Older Emmental tastes stronger.

52588.q: Which milk is Emmental made from?
52588.e: Emmental is made from raw cow's milk. The cows eat grass and hay for it, but no silage.
52588.m: Emmental is made from cow's milk.

52589.q: What shape is a whole wheel of Emmental?
52589.e: A wheel of Emmental is round and flat like a big wheel. That is why people also call it a cheese wheel.
52589.m: A wheel of Emmental is round like a wheel.

52590.q: Which river is the Emmental named after?
52590.e: The Emmental is the valley of the Emme. The Emme flows through the hilly landscape and later joins the Aare.
52590.m: The Emmental is named after the River Emme.

52591.q: When are the cows up on the alpine pasture?
a: In spring, when there is still snow
52591.e: In summer fresh grass grows on the alpine pasture. That is why the cows are taken up into the mountains at this time.
52591.m: In summer the cows are on the alpine pasture.

a: A mountain pasture used in summer
52592.e: An Alp is a pasture in the mountains. Cows, cattle or goats graze there in summer.
52592.m: An Alp is a mountain pasture for the summer.

52593.q: What do cows on the alpine pasture often wear around their necks?
52593.e: The bells ring when the cows walk. That way you can hear where the animals are grazing.
52593.m: Cows on the alpine pasture often wear bells.

52594.q: What is the man called who makes cheese from the milk on the alpine pasture?
52594.e: A Senn or Sennerin (alpine dairy farmer) makes alpine cheese from fresh milk on the alpine pasture.
52594.m: The Senn makes cheese on the alpine pasture.

52595.q: What do the cows on the alpine pasture mainly eat?
52595.e: On the alpine pasture the cows eat fresh grass and lots of mountain herbs. This gives the milk a special taste.
52595.m: On the alpine pasture cows eat grass and herbs.

52596.q: What is the procession of cows up to the alpine pasture in early summer called?
a: The ascent to the alpine pasture
The descent from the alpine pasture
52596.e: In early summer the cows walk from the valley up to the alpine pasture. This is called the ascent, or “Alpaufzug”.
52596.m: During the ascent the cows go up to the alpine pasture.

52597.q: How often a day are dairy cows usually milked?
52597.e: Dairy cows are usually milked in the morning and in the evening, so twice a day.
52597.m: Dairy cows are milked twice a day.

52598.q: What do the Hérens cows in Valais do at a special festival?
52598.e: Hérens cows are strong. In the cow fights they push their heads against each other. The strongest cow becomes queen.
52598.m: Hérens cows test their strength in cow fights.

52599.e: Swiss Brown is one of the most common breeds of cow in Switzerland. The cows are brown and well suited to the mountains.
52599.m: Swiss Brown is a typical Swiss breed of cow.

52600.q: When does the descent from the alpine pasture usually take place?
52600.e: The cows stay on the alpine pasture all summer. Usually in September they return to the valley in a cheerful procession.
52600.m: The descent from the alpine pasture usually takes place in September.

52601.q: What happens during the descent from the alpine pasture?
a: The cows come down to the valley
The cows go up to the alpine pasture
52601.e: During the descent the cows return from the alpine pasture to the valley. There they spend the winter in the shed.
52601.m: During the descent the cows come back to the valley.

52602.q: What are the cows often decorated with during the descent from the alpine pasture?
52602.e: During the descent many cows wear a headdress of flowers and colourful ribbons.
52602.m: During the descent the cows wear flower decorations.

52603.q: Why do the cows leave the alpine pasture in autumn?
a: Because it gets cold up there
Because the pasture gets too small
Because there is a market in the valley
52603.e: In autumn it gets cold in the mountains and snow soon falls. Then hardly any grass grows either.
52603.m: In autumn it gets too cold on the alpine pasture.

52604.q: Which cow often wears the finest decorations during the descent from the alpine pasture?
a: The last cow in the herd
52604.e: The lead cow leads the herd. She often wears the biggest headdress and a big bell.
52604.m: The lead cow walks at the front and is beautifully decorated.

52605.q: What is the descent from the alpine pasture called in French in western Switzerland?
52605.e: In French-speaking Switzerland the descent from the alpine pasture is called “Désalpe”. Some villages hold a big festival for it.
52605.m: In French the descent from the alpine pasture is called Désalpe.

52606.q: What do the alpine herders often wear during the descent from the alpine pasture?
52606.e: During the descent the herdsmen and herdswomen often wear their beautiful traditional costume. That turns the procession into a festival.
52606.m: Many alpine herders wear traditional costume during the descent.

52607.q: What are the big, loud bells that cows wear during the descent from the alpine pasture called?
52607.e: Treicheln are big bells made of sheet metal. They make a loud, deep sound during the descent from the alpine pasture.

52608.q: Where do the cows spend the winter after the descent from the alpine pasture?
a: In the shed in the valley
On the alpine pasture in the snow
On a pasture by the lake
52608.e: After the descent the cows live at the farm in the valley. In winter they eat hay in the shed there.
52608.m: In winter the cows are in the shed in the valley.

52609.q: What colour are many SBB locomotives?
52609.e: Many SBB locomotives and trains are red. The SBB logo is red too.

52610.q: What is the French abbreviation for the SBB (Swiss Federal Railways)?
52610.e: In French the SBB is called “Chemins de fer fédéraux”, CFF for short. In Italian it is called FFS.
52610.m: In French the SBB is called CFF.

52611.q: What is the longest railway tunnel in the world, which is in Switzerland, called?
52611.e: The Gotthard Base Tunnel is about 57 kilometres long. It was opened in 2016 (the longest in the world as of 2026).
52611.m: The Gotthard Base Tunnel is the longest railway tunnel in the world.

52612.q: What is special about the Swiss railway station clock?
a: A Swiss cross in the middle
52612.e: The station clock has a red second hand with a round dot. It stops briefly at the 12.
52612.m: The station clock has a red second hand.

52613.q: Which is the biggest railway station in Switzerland?
52613.e: Huge numbers of trains arrive at and leave Zurich main station every day. It is the biggest station in Switzerland.
52613.m: Zurich main station is the biggest station in Switzerland.

52614.q: What energy do SBB trains run on?
52614.e: SBB trains run on electricity. A large part of the electricity is made with hydropower.

52615.q: What is the travel pass called that lets you use almost all trains for a whole year?
52615.e: With the general travelcard, GA for short, you can use almost all trains, buses and trams in Switzerland.
52615.m: With the GA you can travel almost everywhere in Switzerland.

52616.q: In which year was the SBB founded?
52616.e: The SBB started running in 1902. Before that, the railways belonged to different companies.

52617.q: What is the abbreviation for the Swiss franc?
52617.e: CHF is the abbreviation for the Swiss franc. CH stands for the Latin name of Switzerland.
52617.m: The abbreviation for the franc is CHF.

52618.q: Which is the smallest coin in Switzerland?
52618.e: The smallest coin is the 5-rappen piece. The 1-rappen piece has not been legal tender since 2007.
52618.m: The smallest coin is the 5-rappen piece.

52619.q: What is the big five-franc coin often called?
52619.e: In everyday speech the five-franc coin is called “Fünfliber”. It is the biggest coin in Switzerland.
52619.m: The five-franc coin is called Fünfliber.

52620.q: What colour is the ten-franc note?
52620.e: The ten-franc note is yellow. The other notes have other colours so that you can tell them apart easily.

52621.q: Which note has the highest value in Switzerland?
52621.e: The biggest banknote is the thousand-franc note. There is no five-hundred-franc note.
52621.m: The thousand-franc note is the most valuable note.

52622.q: Which neighbouring country also pays with Swiss francs?
52622.e: Liechtenstein has no currency of its own. People there also pay with Swiss francs.
52622.m: People in Liechtenstein also pay with francs.

52624.q: Which European country do the cities of Ceuta and Melilla on the coast of Morocco belong to?
52624.e: Ceuta and Melilla belong to Spain but lie on the African mainland. Their borders with Morocco are external borders of the EU.
52624.m: Ceuta and Melilla are Spanish cities in Africa.

52625.q: Which oil is made in Morocco from the kernels of a tree that grows almost only there?
52625.e: The argan tree grows almost only in south-west Morocco. Mainly women's cooperatives press the valuable argan oil from the kernels of its fruit.

52626.q: Which large square with street performers and market stalls is Marrakesh famous for?
52626.e: Jemaa el-Fnaa square lies in the old town of Marrakesh. In the evening storytellers, musicians and snake charmers perform there.
52626.m: In Marrakesh, Jemaa el-Fnaa square attracts many visitors.

52627.q: Which part of the Atlas Mountains is the highest?
52627.e: The High Atlas in Morocco has peaks over 4000 metres. The Middle Atlas and the Anti-Atlas are much lower.
52627.m: The High Atlas is the highest part of the mountains.

52628.q: Through which three countries do the Atlas Mountains stretch?
52628.e: The Atlas Mountains stretch for about 2300 kilometres from Morocco through Algeria to Tunisia.
52628.m: The Atlas connects Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia.

52629.q: Which conifer forms large forests in the Middle Atlas?
52629.e: The Atlas cedar forms large forests at heights above 1000 metres. It is also planted as an ornamental tree in Swiss parks.
52629.m: Cedar forests grow in the Middle Atlas.

52630.q: What effect do the Atlas Mountains have on the climate of North Africa?
a: They keep moist sea air away from the Sahara
They bring the Sahara lots of rain
They let glaciers grow down to the sea
They stop all wind on the coast
52630.e: Moist air from the Atlantic rains out on the slopes of the Atlas. South of it, in the rain shadow, the dry Sahara begins.
52630.m: The Atlas separates the wetter coast from the dry Sahara.

52632.q: What is the capital of Algeria?
52632.e: Algiers lies on the Mediterranean coast and is the capital and largest city of the country. The country is named after the city.

52633.q: From which country did Algeria become independent in 1962?
52633.e: Algeria was French for over 130 years. After a long war of independence it became a country of its own in 1962.
52633.m: Algeria became independent from France in 1962.

52634.q: Roughly what share of Algeria's area is part of the Sahara?
52634.e: More than 80 per cent of Algeria is desert. Most people live in the narrow coastal strip on the Mediterranean.

52635.q: What are Algeria's most important exports?
52635.e: Algeria lives mainly from selling oil and natural gas. The gas is also delivered to Europe through pipelines.
52635.m: Algeria mainly exports oil and natural gas.

52636.q: What is Tassili n'Ajjer in Algeria famous for?
a: The highest sand dunes in the world
52636.e: In Tassili n'Ajjer there are thousands of rock pictures showing animals such as giraffes and cattle. They prove that the Sahara used to be green.
52636.m: The rock pictures in Tassili show a once green Sahara.

52637.q: Apart from sand and stony desert, what else is there in the middle of the Algerian Sahara?
52637.e: In the south of Algeria lie the Ahaggar Mountains, also called the Hoggar. Their highest peak is about 2900 metres high.
52637.m: There are high mountains in the middle of the Sahara.

52638.q: What is the currency of Algeria?
52638.e: In Algeria people pay with the Algerian dinar. Tunisia and Libya also have a dinar as their currency.

52639.q: What is the capital of Tunisia?
52639.e: Tunis is the capital and largest city of Tunisia. The country bears the name of its capital.

52640.q: Which ancient city, once an enemy of Rome, lay near present-day Tunis?
52640.e: Carthage was founded by the Phoenicians and fought against Rome in the Punic Wars. Its most famous general was Hannibal.

52641.q: In which country did the protests of the “Arab Spring” begin in 2010/2011?
52641.e: The protests began in Tunisia in December 2010. In January 2011 President Ben Ali had to leave the country.
52641.m: The Arab Spring began in Tunisia.

52642.q: What is the name of the large holiday island in the south of Tunisia?
52642.e: Djerba lies in the Gulf of Gabès and is popular with tourists. It is the largest island in North Africa.

52643.q: Which Roman building stands in the Tunisian town of El Djem?
52643.e: The amphitheatre of El Djem is one of the largest in the Roman world. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
52643.m: A huge Roman amphitheatre stands in El Djem.

52644.q: In which country is the northernmost point of the African mainland?
52644.e: The northernmost point of Africa is a cape near Bizerte in Tunisia. From there it is not far to Sicily.
52644.m: Africa's northern tip is in Tunisia.

52645.q: Which large desert reaches into the south of Tunisia?
52645.e: The south of Tunisia is part of the Sahara, the largest hot desert on Earth. There are sand dunes, oases and large salt lakes there.
52645.m: The Sahara begins in the south of Tunisia.

52646.q: Which European country ruled Tunisia until independence?
52646.e: Tunisia was under French rule from 1881 and became independent in 1956. That is why French is still often spoken there today.
52646.m: Tunisia was under French rule for a long time.

52647.q: What is the capital of Libya?
52647.e: Tripoli lies in the north-west of Libya on the Mediterranean. The second-largest city is Benghazi in the east.

52648.e: Gaddafi came to power in a coup in 1969. In the civil war of 2011 he was overthrown and killed.
52648.m: Gaddafi ruled Libya for over 40 years.

52649.q: Which raw material is most important for Libya's economy?
52649.e: Libya has the largest known oil reserves in Africa. Almost all its export income comes from oil and gas.

52650.q: Which European country ruled Libya as a colony from 1911/1912?
52650.e: Italy conquered Libya in a war against the Ottoman Empire. Italian rule ended after the Second World War.

52651.q: What is the “Great Man-Made River” in Libya?
a: An artificial canal to the sea
52651.e: Huge pipes carry ancient groundwater from the Sahara to the cities on the coast. It is one of the largest water projects in the world.
52651.m: Libya pumps groundwater from the desert to the coast.

52652.q: Which desert covers most of Libya?
52652.e: Over 90 per cent of Libya is desert that is part of the Sahara. Most people live on the Mediterranean coast, for example in Tripoli and Benghazi.
52652.m: Libya is mostly made up of the Sahara.

52653.q: Which people built the great ruined city of Leptis Magna in Libya?
52653.e: Leptis Magna lies east of Tripoli on the Mediterranean and was a rich Roman city. The Roman emperor Septimius Severus was born here.
52653.m: Leptis Magna is a Roman ruined city in Libya.

52654.q: Which peninsula of Egypt is geographically part of Asia?
52654.e: The Sinai Peninsula lies east of the Suez Canal. That is why Egypt is a country on two continents.
52654.m: Sinai is the Asian part of Egypt.

52655.q: Where do most people in Egypt live?
a: In the Nile Valley and Nile Delta
52655.e: About 95 per cent of Egyptians live on a narrow strip along the Nile. The rest of the country is almost all desert.
52655.m: Egyptians live mainly along the Nile.

52656.q: Who founded the city of Alexandria in Egypt?
52656.e: Alexander the Great founded the city in 331 BC in the Nile Delta. It became famous for its library and its lighthouse.
52656.m: Alexandria is named after Alexander the Great.

52657.q: What is the currency of Egypt?
52657.e: In Egypt people pay with the Egyptian pound. One pound is divided into 100 piastres.

52658.q: Which famous structures stand at Giza on the edge of Cairo?
52658.e: The Pyramids of Giza are over 4500 years old. Today they are almost on the edge of the huge city of Cairo.
52658.m: The Pyramids of Giza stand near Cairo.

52659.q: What happened in Tahrir Square in Cairo in 2011?
52659.e: Hundreds of thousands of people gathered in Tahrir Square in 2011. After 18 days of protest, President Hosni Mubarak stepped down.
52659.m: Huge numbers of people protested in Tahrir Square in 2011.

52660.q: Where along the Nile does Cairo lie?
a: At the tip of the Nile Delta
At the source of the Nile
Where the Nile flows into the sea
52660.e: Just north of Cairo the Nile splits into several branches and forms the delta. This location made Cairo an important hub.
52660.m: Cairo lies where the Nile Delta begins.

52661.q: About how many people live in Greater Cairo (as of 2023)?
52661.e: According to UN estimates, about 22 million people lived in Greater Cairo in 2023. That makes it the largest urban area in Africa.
52661.m: Over 20 million people live in Greater Cairo.

52662.q: Which river does the Aswan Dam hold back?
52662.e: The Aswan Dam lies in the south of Egypt on the Nile. It dams the river into a huge lake.
52662.m: The Aswan Dam holds back the Nile.

52663.q: Why were old temples moved when the dams at Aswan were built?
a: They would have sunk in the reservoir
They were in the way of a road
They were to go to a museum in Europe
52663.e: The reservoir flooded large areas along the Nile. With UNESCO's help, temples such as Philae and Abu Simbel were moved to higher places.
52663.m: Because of the reservoir, temples were moved to higher places.

52664.q: In which decade was the Aswan High Dam built?
52664.e: The High Dam was built from 1960 to 1970 with the help of the Soviet Union. A smaller old dam dates back to 1902.
52664.m: The Aswan High Dam was built in the 1960s.

52665.q: Which temples had to be taken apart and rebuilt higher up because of Lake Nasser?
52665.e: Between 1964 and 1968 the rock temples of Abu Simbel were sawn into blocks and rebuilt on a higher site. UNESCO organised the rescue.
52665.m: Abu Simbel was saved from the reservoir.

52666.q: Which yearly natural event on the Nile does the Aswan Dam prevent?
a: The drying out of the delta
52666.e: In the past the Nile flooded the land every year in late summer. The dam holds back this flood water and releases it evenly.
52666.m: The dam stops the yearly Nile flood.

52667.q: What disadvantage do farmers face because the Nile mud stays in the reservoir?
a: Their soil becomes too rich in nutrients
52667.e: In the past the fertile mud fed the fields. Today it settles in Lake Nasser, so farmers have to buy fertiliser.
52667.m: Without Nile mud the fields need fertiliser.

52668.q: Apart from watering fields, what is the water of the Aswan Dam used for?
52668.e: Turbines in the dam generate electricity from water power. As with the reservoirs in the Swiss Alps, the power of falling water is used.
52668.m: The Aswan Dam provides hydroelectric power.

52669.q: What did many people have to do whose villages lay on the Nile above the Aswan High Dam?
a: They had to build boats and live on them
52669.e: Lake Nasser flooded many villages. About 100,000 people in Egypt and Sudan were resettled.
52669.m: Many people had to leave their villages for the reservoir.

52670.q: Which lakes does the Suez Canal pass through on its way?
52670.e: The canal passes through the Great and the Little Bitter Lake. Ships can pass each other there.
52670.m: The Suez Canal crosses the Bitter Lakes.

52672.q: Which town in the middle of the Suez Canal was founded as a workers' town during its construction?
52672.e: Ismailia was founded in 1863 on Lake Timsah and named after the Egyptian ruler Ismail Pasha. Today the canal authority is based there.
52672.m: Ismailia lies in the middle of the Suez Canal.

52673.q: Which French diplomat led the building of the Suez Canal?
52673.e: Ferdinand de Lesseps founded the canal company and pushed the project through. Later he also tried to build the Panama Canal.
52673.m: De Lesseps built the Suez Canal.

52674.q: Which long detour do ships avoid thanks to the Suez Canal?
a: Around the Cape of Good Hope
52674.e: Without the canal, ships from Asia to Europe would have to sail around the whole of Africa. That would be thousands of kilometres more.
52674.m: The Suez Canal saves the journey around Africa.

52675.q: What was opened on the Suez Canal in 2015?
a: A second lane on one section
52675.e: For the so-called “New Suez Canal”, a parallel lane was built along about 35 kilometres. There, ships can travel in both directions at the same time.
52675.m: Since 2015 the Suez Canal has had a second lane on one section.

52676.q: Which country owns the Suez Canal today?
52676.e: In the past the canal was run by a British and French company. Since 1956 it has belonged to Egypt.
52676.m: The Suez Canal belongs to Egypt.

52677.q: Why is the Suez Canal important for Egypt's treasury?
52677.e: Every ship has to pay fees to pass through. This income is one of Egypt's most important sources of foreign currency.
52677.m: The Suez Canal brings Egypt fees.

52678.q: What do you call a river valley in the desert that is usually dry?
52678.e: A wadi only carries water after rare heavy rain. Then dangerous flash floods can suddenly happen.
52678.m: A wadi is a dry river valley in the desert.

52679.q: Where do most oases in the desert get their water from?
52679.e: There is often groundwater under the desert. Where it comes to the surface or is brought up with wells, an oasis forms. Some oases, such as Fayoum in Egypt, get water from the Nile through a canal.

52680.q: What does “layered farming” mean in an oasis?
a: Plants growing at several heights above each other
52680.e: Tall date palms give shade to fruit trees, and vegetables and cereals grow underneath. That way the little water there is gets used well.
52680.m: In layered farming plants grow above each other.

52681.q: Why do some oases lead their water to the fields through underground channels?
a: So that the water stays warm
So that camels cannot drink it
52681.e: In the desert heat, water at the surface evaporates quickly. So long tunnels called foggaras carry the groundwater to the fields under the ground.
52681.m: Underground channels save water in the oasis.

52682.q: What problem arises when an oasis is watered too much and the water evaporates?
52682.e: Water contains dissolved salts. When it evaporates in the heat, the salt stays behind and plants grow less well.
52682.m: Too much watering can make the soil salty.

52684.q: Which fruits grow on the palms in many oases of the Sahara?
52684.e: The date palm is the most important plant in the oases. Its sweet fruits keep for a long time and are an important food.

52685.q: Why are the Tuareg often called the “blue men”?
52685.e: Many Tuareg wear cloths and veils dyed with indigo. The colour sometimes even rubs off onto the skin.
52685.m: The Tuareg often wear indigo-blue veils.

52686.q: Which group of peoples do the Tuareg belong to?
52686.e: The Tuareg are a Berber people. They live in the Sahara and the Sahel, mainly in Niger, Mali, Algeria and Libya.

52687.q: What is the old script of the Tuareg called?
52687.e: The Tifinagh script is made of dots, lines and circles. Today it is also used for other Berber languages.

52688.q: Among the Tuareg, who traditionally covers their face?
52688.e: Unlike in many other societies, among the Tuareg it is the men who wear the veil. The women usually show their faces openly.
52688.m: Among the Tuareg the men wear the veil.

52689.q: Where do the Tuareg mainly live?
a: In the Sahara and the Sahel
On the coast of South Africa
52689.e: The Tuareg live in the Sahara and the Sahel, mainly in Niger, Mali, Algeria and Libya. They speak Tamasheq, a Berber language.
52689.m: The Tuareg live in the Sahara.

52690.q: What does it mean to live as a nomad?
a: To move around without a fixed home
To always live by the sea
52690.e: Nomads move with their herds to pastures and water holes. They take their tents with them.
52690.m: Nomads move around with their animals.

52691.q: Which animal was especially important for the Tuareg in the desert?
52691.e: Dromedaries carry heavy loads and can go a long time without water. With them the Tuareg travelled in caravans through the Sahara, for example to the city of Agadez.
52691.m: The dromedary is the pack animal of the desert.

52692.q: What hit the Sahel especially hard in the 1970s and 1980s?
52692.e: Several years without enough rain made harvests fail and animals die. Many people went hungry or had to leave their homes.

52693.q: What does the Arabic word “Sahel” probably mean?
52693.e: The origin is not completely certain, but “shore” or “coast” is usually given. For travellers from the desert, the Sahel was like the saving shore of the sea of sand.
52693.m: Sahel means shore of the desert.

52694.q: Which plants shape the landscape of the Sahel?
52694.e: Only a little rain falls in the Sahel. So mainly dry grasses, thorn bushes and trees such as acacias and baobabs grow there.
52694.m: Grasses and thorn trees grow in the Sahel.

52695.e: Through droughts, overgrazing and cutting down trees, the soil loses its plant cover. It dries out and turns into desert.

52696.q: Which project aims to create a belt of trees and plants right across the Sahel?
52696.e: The African Union launched the Great Green Wall in 2007. It is meant to stretch from Senegal to Djibouti and stop the desert.
52696.m: The Great Green Wall is meant to make the Sahel green.

52697.q: About how much rain falls in the Sahel each year?
52697.e: In the north of the Sahel about 100 millimetres fall, in the south about 600, mostly in a few summer months. For comparison: Zurich gets over 1000 millimetres a year.
52697.m: The Sahel gets little rain, and only in the rainy season.

52698.q: Which cereal is grown especially often in the Sahel because it copes well with dry weather?
52698.e: Millet needs little water and grows even on poor soil. For many families in the Sahel it is the most important staple food.
52698.m: Millet is the main crop in the Sahel.

52699.q: Which country is part of the Sahel?
52699.e: The Sahel includes Senegal, Mauritania, Mali, Burkina Faso, Niger and Chad, among others. Kenya, Morocco and Angola lie outside it.

52700.q: How many countries border Lake Chad?
52700.e: Lake Chad borders Chad, Niger, Nigeria and Cameroon. Millions of people live from its water and its fish.

52701.q: How has the area of Lake Chad changed since the 1960s?
52701.e: Through droughts and water taken for irrigation, the lake has lost a large part of its open water. About 90 per cent is often mentioned, but this figure is disputed.
52701.m: Lake Chad has shrunk a lot.

a: On the southern edge of the Sahara in Africa
52702.e: Lake Chad lies in Africa where the Sahara meets the Sahel. It is fed mainly by the Chari river.
52702.m: Lake Chad lies on the edge of the Sahara.

52703.q: What is special about Lake Chad compared with Lake Constance?
a: It lies high in the mountains
52703.e: Lake Chad is only a few metres deep. Lake Constance is over 250 metres deep at its deepest point.
52703.m: Lake Chad is a very shallow lake.

52704.q: Where does the water of Lake Chad flow out to?
a: It has no outlet to the sea
52704.e: Lake Chad lies in a basin with no outlet. The water evaporates or seeps away instead of flowing to the sea.
52704.m: Lake Chad has no outlet to the sea.

52705.q: Which country is named after Lake Chad?
52705.e: The country of Chad bears the name of the lake. It lies on the eastern shore and is the largest of the countries around the lake by area.
52705.m: Chad has the same name as the lake.

52706.q: What do many people around Lake Chad live from?
52706.e: Millions of people around Lake Chad fish, grow cereals and keep livestock. Because the lake has shrunk, life there is getting harder.
52706.m: Many people around Lake Chad live from fishing and farming.

52707.q: Which capital city lies close to Lake Chad?
52707.e: N'Djamena, the capital of Chad, lies on the Chari river, not far south of the lake.

52708.q: Where does the Niger rank among the longest rivers in Africa?
52708.e: The Niger is about 4180 kilometres long. Only the Nile and the Congo are longer.
52708.m: The Niger is Africa's third-longest river.

52709.q: What is unusual about the course of the Niger?
a: It first flows away from the sea, inland
52709.e: The Niger rises only about 240 kilometres from the Atlantic but first flows north-east towards the Sahara. Only then does it turn south.
52709.m: The Niger makes a big bend.

52710.q: In which country does the Niger rise?
52710.e: Its source lies in the highlands of Guinea near the border with Sierra Leone.

52711.q: Into which body of water does the Niger flow?
52711.e: The Niger forms a large delta in Nigeria and flows into the Gulf of Guinea, part of the Atlantic.
52711.m: The Niger flows into the Gulf of Guinea.

52712.q: What did the explorer Mungo Park discover on the Niger in 1796?
a: That the river flows into the Nile
That the river dries up in summer
52712.e: Mungo Park reached the Niger at Ségou in present-day Mali. Many Europeans had believed the river flowed west to the Atlantic.

52713.q: Which capital city lies on the Niger?
52713.e: Bamako, the capital of Mali, lies on both banks of the Niger. The capital of the country of Niger also lies on the river.

52714.q: Where is the large inland delta of the Niger?
52714.e: In the inland delta the river splits into many branches and lakes in the middle of the country. It is an important area for fishermen, farmers and migrating birds.
52714.m: The inland delta of the Niger is in Mali.

52715.q: Through which country does the Niger flow on its last stretch to the sea?
52715.e: Finally the Niger flows through Nigeria and forms a large delta there on the Gulf of Guinea. The country of Nigeria is named after the river.
52715.m: The Niger reaches the sea in Nigeria.

52716.q: In which present-day country is Timbuktu?
52716.e: Timbuktu lies in the north of Mali, near the river Niger and on the edge of the Sahara.

52717.q: Which goods were mainly traded in Timbuktu in the Middle Ages?
52717.e: Caravans brought salt from the Sahara, and gold came from the south. This made Timbuktu rich and famous.
52717.m: Timbuktu traded in salt and gold.

52718.q: What is the famous Djinguereber Mosque in Timbuktu built of?
52718.e: The mosque was built of mud around 1327. Wooden beams stick out of the walls so that they can be replastered every year.
52718.m: The great mosque of Timbuktu is made of mud.

52719.q: What was Timbuktu famous for in the 15th and 16th centuries?
52719.e: Many scholars taught in Timbuktu, for example at the Sankore Mosque. Tens of thousands of old manuscripts are still there today.
52719.m: Timbuktu was a city of scholars.

52720.q: On the edge of which desert does Timbuktu lie?
52720.e: Timbuktu lies in the north of Mali on the southern edge of the Sahara. The city has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1988.
52720.m: Timbuktu lies on the edge of the Sahara.

52721.q: What does the saying “from here to Timbuktu” mean?
52721.e: For a long time Europeans saw Timbuktu as a mysterious place that could hardly be reached. That is why the name stands for a very distant place.
52721.m: “From here to Timbuktu” means very far away.

52722.q: How did traders travel through the Sahara to Timbuktu in the past?
a: In sailing ships across the sea
52722.e: Camels can go a long time without water. Traders travelled in caravans with salt, gold and other goods from oasis to oasis.
52722.m: Camel caravans brought goods to Timbuktu.

52723.q: Which country made Accra the capital of its Gold Coast colony in 1877?
52723.e: In 1877 the British moved their seat of government from Cape Coast to Accra. Since independence in 1957, Accra has been the capital of Ghana.
52723.m: Accra was the capital of the British Gold Coast and is now the capital of Ghana.

a: On the banks of the Nile
52724.e: Accra lies right on the Gulf of Guinea, so on the Atlantic. The city is also an important port and trading centre.
52724.m: Accra lies on the Atlantic coast.

52725.q: Which monument in Accra is a reminder of Ghana's independence?
52725.e: The Black Star Gate stands on Independence Square in Accra. The black star is a symbol of Ghana and is also on the flag.
52725.m: The Black Star Gate in Accra recalls independence.

52726.q: Of which country is Accra the capital?
52726.e: Accra lies on the Atlantic coast and is the largest city and capital of Ghana. The second-largest city is Kumasi.
52726.m: Accra is the capital of Ghana.

52727.q: Which huge bronze monument was unveiled in Dakar in 2010?
52727.e: The monument shows a man, a woman and a child and stands on a hill above the city. It is one of the tallest statues in Africa.
52727.m: The African Renaissance Monument stands in Dakar.

52728.q: In which country is the capital Dakar?
52728.e: Dakar is the capital of Senegal. It lies in the far west of Africa on a peninsula in the Atlantic.
52728.m: Dakar is the capital of Senegal.

52729.q: What advantage does Dakar have from its location on the Atlantic?
a: A desert on the edge of town
52729.e: Dakar has one of the most important ports in West Africa. Even countries without a coast, such as Mali, send goods through this port.

52730.q: Which island off Dakar is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a reminder of the slave trade?
52730.e: The small island of Gorée was a European trading post. Today it is a place to remember the slave trade across the Atlantic.
52730.m: The island of Gorée is a reminder of the slave trade.

52731.q: Which city is the capital of the Democratic Republic of the Congo?
52731.e: Kinshasa is the capital and by far the largest city of the country. It is seen as one of the largest French-speaking cities in the world.
52731.m: Kinshasa is the capital of the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

52732.q: What was the Democratic Republic of the Congo called from 1971 to 1997?
52732.e: President Mobutu renamed the country Zaire in 1971. In 1997 it got the name Democratic Republic of the Congo again.
52732.m: The Democratic Republic of the Congo used to be called Zaire.

52733.q: Which great river flows through the Democratic Republic of the Congo?
52733.e: The Congo is the river with the most water in Africa. It gave the country its name.
52733.m: The Congo flows through the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

52734.q: Where does the Democratic Republic of the Congo rank by area in Africa?
52734.e: The Democratic Republic of the Congo covers about 2.3 million square kilometres. Only Algeria is larger in Africa.
52734.m: The Democratic Republic of the Congo is the second-largest country in Africa.

52735.q: Which metal used in batteries is mostly mined in the Democratic Republic of the Congo?
52735.e: More than half of the world's cobalt comes from the south of the country. Cobalt is in many batteries in mobile phones and electric cars.
52735.m: A large part of the world's cobalt comes from the Congo.

52736.q: Which national park in the east of the country is the oldest in Africa and home to mountain gorillas?
52736.e: Virunga National Park was founded in 1925. It protects volcanoes, savannahs and the rare mountain gorillas.
52736.m: Mountain gorillas live in Virunga National Park.

52737.q: Which volcano with a lava lake lies near the city of Goma?
52737.e: Nyiragongo has one of the largest lava lakes on Earth. Its eruptions in 2002 and 2021 threatened the city of Goma.
52737.m: Nyiragongo near Goma has a lava lake.

52738.q: About how long is the sea coast of the Democratic Republic of the Congo?
a: It has no coast at all
52738.e: The huge DR Congo only reaches the Atlantic at the mouth of the Congo. So its coast is only about 40 kilometres long.
52738.m: The DR Congo has only a very short sea coast.

52739.q: Which city is the official capital of the Ivory Coast?
52739.e: Yamoussoukro was declared the capital in 1983. It is the birthplace of the first president.
52739.m: Yamoussoukro is the official capital of the Ivory Coast.

52740.q: Which is the largest city and economic centre of the Ivory Coast?
52740.e: Abidjan lies on a lagoon by the Atlantic and has a large port. Many companies and embassies are based there.
52740.m: Abidjan is the largest city of the Ivory Coast.

52741.q: Where does the Ivory Coast get its name from?
a: From the white houses on the coast
52741.e: European traders used to buy a lot of ivory here, that is, the tusks of elephants. That is how the coast got its name.
52741.m: The Ivory Coast is named after the ivory trade.

52742.q: What is the official French name of the Ivory Coast?
52742.e: The country wants its name to be written in French in all languages. Côte means coast and ivoire means ivory.
52742.m: The Ivory Coast is officially called Côte d'Ivoire.

52743.q: What kind of huge building stands in Yamoussoukro and is reminiscent of St Peter's Basilica in Rome?
52743.e: The Basilica of Our Lady of Peace was consecrated in 1990. It is one of the largest churches in the world.
52743.m: One of the largest churches in the world stands in Yamoussoukro.

52744.q: From which country did the Ivory Coast become independent in 1960?
52744.e: The Ivory Coast was a French colony and became independent in 1960. That is why French is still an official language today.
52744.m: The Ivory Coast was a French colony until 1960.

52745.q: Which national park in Côte d’Ivoire is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and known for chimpanzees that use tools?
52745.e: In the rainforest of Taï National Park, chimpanzees crack nuts with stones and pieces of wood. The park protects one of the last large rainforests in West Africa.
52745.m: In Taï National Park, chimpanzees use tools.

52746.q: What is the nickname of Côte d’Ivoire’s national football team?
52746.e: The elephant is the national animal on Côte d’Ivoire’s coat of arms. That is why the national team is called “Les Éléphants”, the Elephants.
52746.m: Côte d’Ivoire’s footballers are called “Les Éléphants”.

52747.q: Which city is the capital of Gabon?
52747.e: Libreville lies on the coast in the north-west of Gabon. The name means “free town”, because freed slaves were settled here.
52747.m: Libreville is the capital of Gabon.

52748.q: How much of Gabon’s land is covered by rainforest?
52748.e: Gabon is one of the most forested countries on Earth. More than 70 per cent of its land is tropical rainforest.
52748.m: Gabon is mostly covered by rainforest.

52749.q: What is the doctor Albert Schweitzer known for in Gabon?
a: He founded a hospital in the jungle
52749.e: In 1913 Albert Schweitzer opened a jungle hospital in Lambaréné and treated sick people there. He later received the Nobel Peace Prize.
52749.m: Albert Schweitzer founded a jungle hospital in Gabon.

52750.q: Into which ocean does the Ogooué, Gabon’s most important river, flow?
52750.e: Gabon lies on the west coast of Africa. The Ogooué, about 1200 kilometres long, flows into the Atlantic there.
52750.m: The Ogooué flows into the Atlantic.

52751.q: Which raw material earns Gabon the most export income?
52751.e: About four fifths of export income comes from oil. Manganese and timber are also exported.
52751.m: Gabon earns the most from oil.

52752.q: What is the official language of Gabon?
52752.e: Gabon was a French colony and became independent in 1960. In everyday life many people also speak Bantu languages such as Fang.
52752.m: French is the official language of Gabon.

52753.q: What is Loango National Park in Gabon known for?
a: Forest animals such as elephants on the beach
52753.e: In Loango National Park the rainforest reaches right down to the sea. That is why you can see elephants, buffalo and hippos on the beach there.
52753.m: In Loango National Park, forest animals come down to the beach.

52754.q: What was discovered at Oklo in Gabon?
a: Natural nuclear reactors from ancient times
The largest cave in the world
52754.e: About two billion years ago, chain reactions took place on their own in uranium deposits near Oklo. French scientists discovered this in 1972.
52754.m: There were natural nuclear reactors at Oklo.

52755.q: Which people in Ghana honour a Golden Stool as the sacred symbol of their kingdom?
52755.e: For the Ashanti, the Golden Stool is the seat of the soul of the whole people. Nobody may sit on it, not even the king.
52755.m: The Golden Stool is the sacred symbol of the Ashanti.

52756.q: Which fortress did the Portuguese build in 1482 on the coast of present-day Ghana?
52756.e: Elmina Castle is thought to be the oldest European building south of the Sahara. Later it was a place of the slave trade, and today it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
52756.m: Elmina fortress in Ghana dates from 1482.

52757.q: From which country did Ghana become independent in 1957?
52757.e: As the Gold Coast, Ghana was a British colony. Under Kwame Nkrumah it became independent in 1957, one of the first countries in Africa to do so.

52758.q: What is the colourful cloth from Ghana woven in strips called?
52758.e: Kente is woven from narrow strips that are sewn together. Every colour and every pattern has its own meaning.
52758.m: Kente is a colourful woven cloth from Ghana.

52759.q: What was Ghana called when it was still a British colony?
52759.e: Because of the rich gold deposits, Europeans called the area the Gold Coast. Since independence in 1957 the country has been called Ghana.
52759.m: Ghana used to be called the Gold Coast.

52760.q: Which ocean does the Gulf of Guinea belong to?
52760.e: The Gulf of Guinea is a large bay on the west coast of Africa. It is part of the Atlantic Ocean.
52760.m: The Gulf of Guinea is part of the Atlantic.

52761.q: Which two important lines of the global grid cross in the Gulf of Guinea?
52761.e: At the point with 0 degrees latitude and 0 degrees longitude, the Equator and the Prime Meridian meet. This point lies in the open sea of the Gulf of Guinea.
52761.m: The Equator and the Prime Meridian cross in the Gulf of Guinea.

52762.q: What is special about Malabo, the capital of Equatorial Guinea?
a: It lies on an island in the sea
It lies in the middle of the desert
It lies high in the mountains
It lies on a large inland lake
52762.e: Malabo lies on the volcanic island of Bioko in the Gulf of Guinea. The mainland of Equatorial Guinea lies further south-east.
52762.m: Malabo lies on an island in the Gulf of Guinea.

52763.q: Which small island country lies in the Gulf of Guinea?
52763.e: São Tomé and Príncipe consists of two main islands of volcanic origin. It is one of the smallest countries in Africa.
52763.m: São Tomé and Príncipe is an island country in the Gulf of Guinea.

52764.q: Which big river forms a huge delta on the Gulf of Guinea?
52764.e: In Nigeria the Niger splits into many branches before it flows into the sea. Its delta is one of the largest in the world.
52764.m: The Niger flows into the Gulf of Guinea with a huge delta.

52765.q: Which raw material is mainly extracted in the Niger Delta and off the coast of the Gulf of Guinea?
52765.e: Large deposits of oil and natural gas lie under the seabed and in the delta. Countries such as Nigeria, Angola and Gabon earn a lot of money from them.
52765.m: A lot of oil is extracted in the Gulf of Guinea.

52766.q: Which problem has threatened ships in the Gulf of Guinea for years?
52766.e: Armed groups attack ships and kidnap sailors. The Gulf of Guinea is seen as one of the most dangerous sea regions for shipping.
